# ModWorld — 2.5D 3/4 pixel art และ VFX production plan

วันที่: 2026-10-27  
สถานะ: ทิศทางภาพ 2.5D pixel ล็อกแล้ว; งานทั้งหมดเป็น sprite/atlas 2D ที่ใช้ arena projection เดิม

**แผนนี้เป็นงาน 2.5D pixel art**: ตัวละคร อุปกรณ์ mob และ VFX เป็นภาพ pixel ที่วาด/เจนเป็น sprite และ atlas 2D แล้วประกอบบน ground plane ด้วย projection เดิมของ arena. ไม่มี geometry, rig, mesh หรือ renderer ใหม่ใน runtime; ภาพ concept และ sprite sheet เป็น deliverable ของงานนี้. ห้ามเริ่มผลิตทั้ง roster ก่อน proof ผ่าน.

**เมื่อ replacement ผ่าน QA และใช้งานร่วมกับ runtime ได้ ให้ integrator เปิดใช้เป็น default ของส่วนนั้นทันที ไม่ต้องรอทั้ง roster หรือขออนุมัติรายชิ้นซ้ำ**. ระบบเดิมที่ยังไม่ถูกแทนยังทำงานต่อ; ห้ามลบหรือทำให้ fallback เสีย.

## 1. Visual direction และ proof

### ภาพและสไตล์ที่ผู้ใช้เลือก

[ภาพนักธนูที่อนุมัติเป็น style reference](../../art-reference/players/pixel-archer-direction-concept-2026-10-27.png) ล็อกงาน pixel art รายละเอียดระดับภาพนี้: เส้นผม ผ้า หนัง อุปกรณ์ และ shading ที่มีมิติ; สัดส่วน chibi เล็กน้อย ใบหน้าแสดงอารมณ์และ silhouette ชัด ไม่บังคับลดรายละเอียดให้ pixel หยาบขึ้น ตรวจความอ่านออกที่ขนาดเล่นจริง

[Minotaur ที่มีอยู่](../../art-reference/monsters/minotaur/animation/source/base.png) เป็น reference ของ mob รูปร่างกะทัดรัด แข็งแรง ใบหน้าและอาวุธอ่านชัด รักษาสัดส่วน บุคลิก และความน่าเกรงขามเฉพาะของ mob แต่ละชนิด ให้ player และ mob อยู่ในโลกภาพเดียวกัน ไม่ทำทุกตัวเป็นของเล่นหน้าตาเหมือนกัน หลีกเลี่ยงตัวละครกล่อง voxel, ภาพมันวาว และภาพเบลอแทน pixel

ภาพนักธนูเป็น first-party concept สำหรับสไตล์; ชุดและสีเป็นตัวอย่าง ไม่ใช่เครื่องแบบของทุกตัวละคร

### โลก กล้อง และ gameplay

โลกเป็น 2.5D: ground plane หน่วยเมตร + sprite ที่มีความสูงเป็นภาพ; กล้อง 3/4 คงที่ตาม player ไม่ตาม target. ใช้ projection ของแต่ละ domain ตามของเดิม — arena ใช้ matrix จาก `ARENA_*` ใน `game/src/presentation/arena-camera.ts` และ map ใช้ `createMapProjection` (elevation 38°, yaw −16°) ใน `game/src/ui/map/map-projection.ts`; ห้ามสร้างกล้องใหม่หรือเปลี่ยน projection เพื่อให้ภาพง่ายขึ้น

Actor ใช้ 8 world directions ตาม `ARENA_DIRECTIONS`; sprite มี anchor/socket/visible bounds ชัด; body footprint 0.5 m diameter; field 50 m. Gameplay timing, committed geometry และ actual receipts ยังเป็น authority; ภาพไม่เพิ่ม hit, timer, proc, reward หรือ RNG.

### ลำดับงานภาพที่ล็อก

1. **Character:** ผลิต sprite/animation ของตัวละครผู้เล่นทั้งหมดและ equipment layers ที่จำเป็น เริ่มจาก archer เป็นตัวแทน pipeline; version ที่ผ่าน QA เปิด default ทันที
2. **Mob:** ผลิต sprite/animation ของ mob ทั้ง roster เริ่มจาก minotaur เป็นตัวแทน; รักษาขนาดและบุคลิกของแต่ละ species
3. **Skill VFX:** ผลิต/ปรับ authored pixel VFX ครบตาม live roster และ basic/mob paths โดยอิง `game/public/fx/skill-pool/vfx-production.md`; ใช้ canonical action/area/timing
4. **Map / terrain / environment:** ทำเป็นลำดับสุดท้าย คงของปัจจุบันไว้ระหว่างทาง; ใช้ terrain slice จริง 1–2 hex ใน proof เพื่อ calibrate scale

Phase 1 ปล่อยเป็น slice: proof → 1 actor + 1 mob → ต่อ class/family; ห้ามเริ่ม batch ถัดไปก่อน slice ก่อนหน้าผ่าน checklist/capture/budget.

### Proof ก่อนยกเครื่องทั้งเกม

1. ทำ archer พร้อม bow, mob ตัวแทน และ terrain slice จริง 1–2 hex พร้อมความสูง 0–2 ระดับ ในสไตล์ที่เลือก ให้เห็น idle → draw → release → flight → contact
2. ใช้ `attack.piercing_shot`: ลูกศรหนึ่งดอกตามแนวที่ commit ความยาว 5.2 m และ full width 0.75 m ตาม `tools/data/skills.json`; contact เฉพาะ recipient จริง ไม่ใช้ beam เต็มเส้นหรือลูกศรหลายดอกแทน hit เพิ่ม
3. Proof set ต้องมี: Piercing Shot, Cleave (sector 120°), persistent field 1 ตัว, aura 1 ตัว, channel/mobile effect 1 ตัว และ overlap scene ที่มี 2–3 effect พร้อม mob หลายตัว; ทดสอบที่ 8 world directions และมุมกลางระหว่าง bin
4. ตรวจใน browser ที่ 1920 × 1080 ด้วย arena camera matrix: alignment, height/depth, footprint, readability, reduced motion และ pixel stability (ไม่มี shimmer/crawl เกิน 1 native pixel)
5. วัดและบันทึก frame time p50/p95, heap, และ native resolution/upscale; production gate คือ 60 Hz floor (p95 16.8 ms, owner-accepted 2026-10-27) และห้ามใช้ dev showcase ที่มี debug overhead เป็นหลักฐาน
6. **ล็อก native resolution และ upscale factor** ใน decision record หลัง proof; เปลี่ยนค่าหลังล็อก = re-run proof
7. ถ้า proof ไม่ผ่าน budget ใช้ degraded tiers: ลด decorative density/quality → ลด directions ของ ambient/decor → ลด component ที่ไม่ใช่ cue หลัก → คง fallback เดิมของส่วนนั้น; ห้ามลดพื้นที่ cue หลักหรือเปลี่ยน gameplay shape

## 2. ขอบเขตและ ownership

- Canonical gameplay, skill identity และ save identity คงเดิม; presentation ไม่สร้าง damage, hits, timers หรือ RNG. งาน engine/runtime ใช้ [engine implementation plan](engine-implementation-work.md) เป็น contract
- **Image/2D asset generation เป็นของ art owner:** agent ไม่เจนภาพหรือแก้ asset; agent ตรวจ validator/tests/integration และหยุด/report ถ้า asset ขาด
- Art owner ส่ง source/candidate, provenance, native scale, anchor/socket, animation metadata, budgets และวิธี reproduce; integrator ผูก runtime และเลือก candidate ที่ผ่าน
- ใช้ first-party art; ไม่เพิ่ม third-party asset packs หรือ external generation services. งานภาพทุกชิ้นต้องมี provenance และ version
- Runtime renderer, camera และ projection เดิมเป็น authority; งานนี้ไม่เพิ่ม renderer/dependency ใหม่

### Versioned asset pool

- จัดงานแยกตาม subject/component และเก็บ candidate ใน `v1/`, `v2/`; player, mob, equipment, skill และ map มี identity/version ของตัวเอง
- Source/candidate อยู่ใต้ `art-reference/` ตาม subject; runtime อยู่ใต้ `game/src/ui/combat/arena/` สำหรับ actor art และ `game/public/fx/skill-pool/<skill-slug>/vN/` สำหรับ skill VFX; ห้ามใช้ path เดิมทับ version ที่ส่งแล้ว
- ใช้ lowercase hyphens; skill ใช้ slug เดิม เช่น `attack-piercing-shot`; 2D atlas metadata/QA ใช้ `game/public/fx/skill-pool/vfx-production.md` และ `tools/check-authored-vfx.py`
- Candidate ใหม่สร้าง version ใหม่; ระบุสถานะ `draft | candidate | accepted | selected | retired`; แยก review จาก default selection
- Integrator เปิด selected version เป็น default ราย slice; เก็บ version เดิมเป็น fallback; art version ไม่เปลี่ยน skill/save identity

## 3. Asset brief ก่อนผลิตแต่ละ component

ระบุ canonical skill/component, gameplay shape/origin/delivery/timestamps, actor/equipment reference, camera/native resolution, footprint, frame grid, anchor/socket, animation states, depth/layer order, reduced-motion variant, budget (texture size, frames, file size), provenance และ rejection criteria. Particle distribution ตามพื้นที่ ไม่ใช่จำนวน target; แยก component ตาม phase/motion/path.

## 4. 2.5D production contract

- Sprite/atlas ต้องอ่าน silhouette, pixel clusters, materials และ luminous core ได้ที่ขนาดเล่นจริง; การลด resolution อย่างเดียวไม่รับประกันคุณภาพ
- Cone/line/projectile/field แสดง full footprint/trajectory ตาม committed area; empty ground ต้องเห็น; hit เกิดตาม receipt จริง
- Anchor/socket/visible bounds ต้องตรงระหว่าง actor, weapon และ effect; depth order ตาม ground plane; ห้ามฝัง actor/weapon ใน effect ที่ต้องแยก
- One-shot/pulse/loop/exit/interruption ตรง lifecycle จริง; decoration ไม่เพิ่ม hit หรือบดบังพื้นที่สำคัญ; fallback ทำงานเมื่อ candidate ผิด/ไม่ผ่าน
- Reduced motion ยังคงพื้นที่และ cue สำคัญ; ไม่มี shimmer/crawl เกิน 1 native pixel

## 5. Skill VFX contracts

รายละเอียดราย skill และ QA อยู่ที่ [authored VFX production](../../game/public/fx/skill-pool/vfx-production.md) และ atlas ต่อ skill; ตารางนี้เป็น contract ระดับ family:

| Family                                                                                                                    | ภาพ/จังหวะที่ต้องส่ง                                                                        | Reject                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Melee/cone/line (Cleave, Impale, Venom Spray, Shield Bash, Ground Slam, Whirlwind, Piercing Shot)                         | weapon/emitter sweep หรือ thrust ตาม committed sector/line; contact ต่อ actual recipient    | วงเต็ม, ทิศตาม target หลัง lock, contact ด้านหลัง                          |
| Burst/projectile (Water Ball, Double Strike, Split Shot, Ice Lance, Arrow Shower, Chain Lightning, Overload)              | จำนวนลูก/จังหวะตาม canonical row; one aim/one cast; contact แยกตาม receipt                  | one projectile + fake flashes, clone slash พร้อมกัน, ลูกศรตั้งแต่ release  |
| Fields/nova/status/aura (Storm Field, Poison Cloud, Blizzard, Sand Storm, Firestorm, Meteor, novae, buff/curse/heal/aura) | bed/field ตาม footprint และ duration จริง; pulse/aura loop; status accent ตาม first-success | field ที่ดู damage ตลอด, cloud ตาม target, aura ring กลายเป็น enemy radius |
| Basic/mob paths                                                                                                           | ใช้ contract เดียวกัน; mob skill ต้องอ่านทิศ/พื้นที่จริง                                    | coverage จาก manifest entry โดยไม่มี runtime หลักฐาน                       |

- Burst budget ใช้ count × authored share จริง; cosmetic fragments ไม่เพิ่ม hit
- Field: 1 active instance ต่อ caster+skill+arena; pulse ตาม absolute schedule; recast replace future work โดยไม่ refund
- Contact/impact/status อ่าน receipt จริง; visual cue ไม่สร้าง gameplay

## 6. Density และ timing

### 6.1 Visual timing envelope

| Family                  | Primary cue                         | Tail/ambient                      |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Single melee cut/thrust | 100–160 ms active, contact 60–90 ms | trail dissolve 80–140 ms          |
| Shield/blunt            | contact 60–100 ms                   | recoil/particles 120–180 ms       |
| Venom Spray             | fan burst 160–240 ms                | droplets 120–180 ms               |
| Ground burst/nova/slam  | footprint peak 180–260 ms           | dust/cracks 250–450 ms            |
| Single projectile       | release 30–50 ms                    | impact 60–100 ms, exit 100–160 ms |
| Chain                   | one link ต่อ hop                    | decay 60–100 ms                   |
| Persistent field        | activation 180–250 ms               | bed/wind loop 0.8–1.6 s           |
| Mobile channel          | rotation ตลอด channel               | finish 120–180 ms                 |
| Buff/curse              | activation 180–250 ms               | exit 120–180 ms                   |
| Aura                    | enable cue                          | orbit 1.8 s, breathing 2.4 s      |

ค่าเหล่านี้เป็น presentation tuning ไม่ใช่ gameplay timing; runtime อ่าน resolved timestamps จริง

### 6.2 Density

```text
referenceArea = PI * 3m * 3m
densityScale = min(actualWorldArea / referenceArea, 2)
ambientBirthRate = familyBaseRate * densityScale * qualityMultiplier
activeCosmeticCap = ceil(familyBaseCap * densityScale * qualityMultiplier)
```

- `actualWorldArea`: circle πR², cone αR²/2 (radians), line L×W
- Quality: standard 1 / low 0.5; ลดเฉพาะ decoration ไม่ลด field bed/real pulse cue
- Cap เฉพาะ weather/decorative particles ไม่ใช่ hit recipients
- Budget รวมทั้ง arena: active cosmetic particles ≤ 2,000 และ effect instances ≤ 120 ที่ standard; stress scene = mob cap + 3 field + weather 1 ระบบ
- Birth schedule จาก absolute sim time + index + stable cosmetic seed; seek/resume ไม่ปล่อย backlog

## 7. QA และ acceptance

- ตรวจ source/atlas: alpha, cell grid, anchors, sockets, animation frames, metadata และ provenance; `python tools/check-authored-vfx.py --selected` สำหรับ selected VFX
- ตรวจใน arena/browser จริงที่ 1920 × 1080 ด้วย arena matrix: actor-to-area ratio, 8 world directions + mid-angle, motion/weapon alignment, center-to-edge coverage, empty ground, contact timing เทียบ receipt, overlap/occlusion, readability, interruption และ reduced motion
- ตรวจ pixel art ที่ native res และเทียบ reference; ภาพนิ่ง/lab preview เพียงอย่างเดียวไม่ผ่าน
- Performance: production live p50/p95, heap, device/browser; gate 60 Hz floor (p95 ≤16.8 ms, owner-accepted); dev showcase debug ไม่ใช่หลักฐาน
- Automated capture: screenshot ต่อ skill × 8 direction + mid-angle ที่ seed/เวลาเดิม เก็บ artifact คู่ version
- Mixed 2.5D slices ต้องผ่าน visual coherence check; rollback version ก่อนได้ทันที

## 8. Definition of done

- Proof มี character/mob/terrain slice, skill set, runtime integration และ provenance ที่ทำซ้ำได้ พร้อม browser evidence
- Pixel appearance และ chibi detail สอดคล้อง reference; camera และ 8 ทิศ + มุมกลางอ่าน action ได้
- Anchor/socket/depth/full area/timing/contact/cancellation/reduced motion ผ่าน; ไม่เพิ่ม gameplay effects
- Performance และ selected versions/paths/checks/limits ถูกบันทึก; 2.5D ที่ยัง pending แยกจากของเดิมชัดเจน
- ลำดับ Character → Mob → Skill VFX → Map ครบ; ไม่มี geometry/runtime renderer ใน pipeline

# ModWorld — agent working agreement

Single-player, browser-only idle RPG; no server. This is the shared entry point for every coding agent.

## Document map

| Source                                                          | Owns                                                                                                                                                                                   | Read when                                                                                                                                                            |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `AGENTS.md`                                                     | Workflow, ownership, commands and verification                                                                                                                                         | Starting work; reuse once loaded                                                                                                                                     |
| `docs/glossary.md`                                              | Short definitions of game terms                                                                                                                                                        | A term is ambiguous, new or renamed                                                                                                                                  |
| `docs/map-art.md`                                               | Map terrain artwork contract and the projected ground footprint                                                                                                                        | Producing or placing terrain hex art                                                                                                                                 |
| `art-reference/`                                                | Portable map art reference kit, generated-image holding area awaiting approval, concept images and map calibration snapshots; never imported by game runtime (dev review + tests only) | Generating, measuring or QC-ing map art; generated files are not game-ready until approved and copied into game assets; refresh with `art-reference/map/refresh.ps1` |
| `art/`                                                          | Generated gallery output (`gallery.html`, `favs.json` queue); never hand-edited, rebuilt by `tools/gallery.ts`                                                                         | Reviewing shelf sheets in a browser                                                                                                                                  |
| `game/src/assets/`                                              | Runtime non-shelf images (backgrounds, skins); not keyed by the icon resolver                                                                                                          | Adding a non-glyph runtime image                                                                                                                                     |
| `tools/data/*.json`                                             | Numbers, tuning, catalogues and content                                                                                                                                                | Changing or tracing those values                                                                                                                                     |
| `engine/`, `game/src/`                                          | Implementation, interfaces and UI appearance                                                                                                                                           | Working on the affected code                                                                                                                                         |
| `game/src/icon/`                                                | Art shelf for item, skill, mob, UI and map-glyph images; folders group by subject and resolvers key on the file name                                                                   | Adding or sorting artwork                                                                                                                                            |
| `game/src/ui/combat/arena/`, `game/src/ui/combat/fx-manifests/` | Runtime animation + VFX manifests embedded by import; data, not shelf art                                                                                                              | Changing arena animation or authored VFX                                                                                                                             |
| `game/src/wiki/pages.ts`                                        | Player-facing wiki source                                                                                                                                                              | Changing what the wiki explains                                                                                                                                      |

Each fact has one owner. Link to it rather than copying it. Provider entry files import or point here; they carry no separate project rules.

## Default working skill

For repository implementation, fixes, reviews and investigation, apply [lean-agent](.agents/skills/lean-agent/SKILL.md) by default. Read it once when needed; reuse it if already loaded. No manual invocation is required. Explicit user requests for another approach or more detail take precedence. Tool policy stays here; the skill owns implementation and communication habits.

## Scope and documentation

- The current user request can change earlier design choices. Documents describe the current design, not permanent restrictions. Do not ask again solely because a requested change differs from an old design.
- UI-only work starts from components/styles and does not require formula or game-rule documents.
- Keep UI appearance and placement in code. Do not document button positions, colours, spacing, control inventories or other changing visual details.
- Edit docs only when requested, or when this task changes a documented formula, term, behavior contract or integration point that future work relies on. Patch that section only; no incidental reorganization, changelogs or unrelated rewrites.
- Skills and audit prompts follow this scope; they create no extra approval steps, documentation work or redesigns outside the task.
- Production art and art generation are first-party. Do not add third-party asset packs or external generation services (for example PixelLab). Existing imported reference packs stay as reference/placeholder only unless the user asks to remove them.
- Active-skill VFX follows [the authored VFX production queue](game/public/fx/skill-pool/vfx-production.md). The user requested the listed 23 attack skills completed and integrated together, without per-skill approval; skills outside that batch retain their existing effects.
- Work only in the active workspace/sandbox and on files supplied for the task. The current local files are the source of truth. Do not inspect Git state, history, branches, remotes or other worktrees; do not compare the workspace with committed content.
- Preserve in-flight changes. Plan briefly for risky/cross-layer work; implement straightforward changes directly. Delegate only independent work with nonoverlapping ownership when delegation is authorized.
- Ask about unclear scope, new dependencies, destructive operations or unsafe/lossy compatibility changes. Routine choices and explicitly requested design changes need no extra approval.

## Tool calls

- Before calling, identify the missing fact or required action and how its result advances the task. Use existing evidence when sufficient; keep this reasoning internal.
- Start with the relevant path/symbol and a bounded output. Exclude dependencies, generated output and logs unless implicated. Read matching sections; expand only when evidence calls for it.
- Reuse verified reads and passing checks until affected inputs change or a concrete uncertainty remains. Do not poll unchanged state without a reason.
- Batch independent searches/reads in one call and inspect each result. Run dependent actions sequentially; do not create unnecessary parallel work.
- If output is truncated, narrow the query or select a useful slice. On failure, identify the cause before retrying; retry only with a changed approach or new evidence. Repeated failure without new evidence calls for reassessment or a blocker report.
- A failing check outside the changed surface, with no changed input that explains it, is baseline or in-flight work: report it and do not fix or rerun it repeatedly without new evidence or a user request. Preserve concurrent edits in shared files; if verification cannot be made repeatable, say so instead of treating the result as a regression.
- Follow the verification scope below. Stop when acceptance criteria and required checks are satisfied. Review an unexpectedly long tool sequence for avoidable work; a call count never justifies skipping essential verification.

## Temporary files and cleanup

- Prefer direct commands and in-memory processing. Create temporary files only when required by a tool or when they materially simplify the task.
- Put temporary files in one task-specific directory under the operating system's temporary directory, within permitted filesystem boundaries. If that location is unavailable, use one task-specific temporary directory inside the active workspace. Do not scatter scripts, screenshots, reports, logs or scratch files throughout the workspace.
- Keep requested deliverables in their intended project locations; do not treat them as temporary files.
- Track temporary files and background processes created during the task. Remove temporary files when no longer needed and before finishing; stop task-created helper processes when no longer needed. Keep services needed to use the requested result running and report them at handoff.
- Delete only files or directories created by the current task. Before recursive deletion, verify the resolved absolute target is inside the task's temporary directory. Never use broad cleanup patterns or delete pre-existing files as housekeeping.
- Do not create transcript files, duplicate source copies, backup files or permanent helper scripts unless the task requires them.
- Before finishing, review task-created artifacts and remove unused files. Report any temporary files or helper processes that could not be cleaned up, including their locations or identifiers and the reason.
- Efficiency and cleanup must not skip required verification or compromise existing work.

## Code and data ownership

| Location                                | Responsibility                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `engine/`                               | Shared formulas and data-driven mechanics                                                                                                                                                |
| `tools/data/engine.json`                | Stats, combat, loot, craft, mobs/zones, inventory, fieldwork and dungeon configuration                                                                                                   |
| `tools/data/spawns.json`                | Field spawn layout, population cap, per-slot respawn, aggro/assist/leash ranges and offline engagement share                                                                             |
| `tools/data/mods.json`                  | Mod ranges, quality bands and drop weights                                                                                                                                               |
| `tools/data/town.json`                  | Town stock/prices, Standing, Collector, tasks, trade, Haggling, Delivery and Black Market                                                                                                |
| `tools/data/skills.json`                | Skill roster, reserve tiers and skill configuration                                                                                                                                      |
| `tools/data/mob-skills.json`            | Mob-only skill library and the Unique/Boss/Variant/Species override kits                                                                                                                 |
| `tools/data/tree.json`                  | Passive-tree specification                                                                                                                                                               |
| `tools/data/tree-retired-baseline.json` | Frozen legacy retired node ids; update only for an intentional save migration                                                                                                            |
| `tools/data/bases.json`                 | Hand-maintained frames, slots and Mod pools; never generate by parsing docs                                                                                                              |
| `tools/data/map.json`                   | Presentation map layout, terrain and colours; never import in `engine/` or `game/src/`                                                                                                   |
| `tools/`                                | Cages, reports and shared readers; `tools/map.ts` generates the overlay                                                                                                                  |
| `art/`                                  | Generated gallery output (`gallery.html`, `favs.json` queue); never hand-edited, rebuilt by `tools/gallery.ts`                                                                           |
| `game/src/assets/`                      | Runtime non-shelf images (backgrounds, skins); not keyed by the icon resolver                                                                                                            |
| `game/src/engine/client.ts`             | Browser bridge to canonical JSON and shared engine factories                                                                                                                             |
| `game/src/sim/`                         | Runtime composition/state; `core/` sheet+loop, `combat/` fights+skills, `town/` markets+contracts, `gear/` loot+craft, `world/` map+field; `core/player.ts` composes the character sheet |
| `game/src/state/save.ts`                | Save loading, migration and persistence                                                                                                                                                  |
| `game/src/ui/`, `game/src/App.svelte`   | Components and application wiring                                                                                                                                                        |

Gameplay numbers live in data JSON, formulas in `engine/`; do not duplicate either in the client. New game-content filenames use lowercase hyphens. `skill.md`, `skills.md`, `SKILL.md` and `.opencode/skills/` are reserved for agent skills, not game content. Gate output is the run record; do not create transcript files.

## Passive-tree node generation

Plan the route before adding the node. For every new or moved node, state its purpose — route, two-anchor loop, junction, or leaf — and the anchors it serves. A count ("15 per wing", "five per cluster") is an output of the design, never the reason to add a node.

- A live leaf must be a Notable or a Keystone. An ordinary node with one connection is filler; the build retires it and `TR17` fails the tree.
- Every live Normal must sit on a route between two anchors (Start, Notable, Keystone, Junction). A loop or run hanging off a single point with no anchor inside it is filler, even when every node has two connections.
- A Keystone is a leaf off exactly one Notable; it is never a through-route. A second Keystone may share that Notable's pocket, but never a route.
- Never add a node for the build to retire. The retired ids in `tools/data/tree-retired-baseline.json` are frozen save keys; a new retired id fails `TR18`.
- Run `node tools/tree.ts --checks` after the build; `TR17`–`TR19` are the purpose, retirement and keystone-leaf gates.

## UI integration

- Shared tokens: `game/src/styles/variables.css`; tag defaults: `base.css`; reusable appearance: `skins.css`; layout: component `<style>`. Read relevant tokens and the existing component. Keep static appearance in classes; inline bindings are for runtime values and HudLayout placement.
- UI icons use PNG shelf art drawn through `.icon-mask` so they keep `currentColor`; map glyphs use PNG shelf art inside the map SVG. Inline SVG remains for structural graphics (tree/map geometry, marker frames/leaders, charts, effects), not standalone UI icons.
- Map markers are a shelf PNG glyph in a circular medallion on a vertical leader from the hex centre; frame and leader use the hover-hex blue (`--es`). Never repaint terrain for marker work.
- Current shell: fixed 15 × 15 Hub Grid, shared `HudLayout` regions and one scroll owner per region. Added/moved regions update `HudRegionId`, `HUD_REGION_META`, `DEFAULT_HUD_LAYOUT` in `game/src/ui/hud/hud-layout.ts` and matching `App.svelte` wiring; backfill old saved layouts. Appearance inside regions follows the requested design.
- New panels connect through `PANELS`, `RAIL`, icon/label maps and keyboard actions in `App.svelte`. Reuse existing shared controls such as `CollapseToggle.svelte` where appropriate; choose Grid/Flex and composition for the task.
- Keep native semantics, labels, keyboard access and visible focus. Map arrows select adjacent Blocks; Enter walks or uses a known Waypoint, with selection announcements.
- Inspect actual components with HMR in the integrated browser at `http://localhost:5173/__showcase#showcase-field`, **1920 × 1080 only** unless another viewport is requested. Use one visible tab; close it after verification. Playwright is not installed in this repository — never launch a standalone/headless browser or build a mirror; verify UI with the dev server, focused tests and `npm --prefix game run check`, using whichever browser the session already provides, and report the failure if none is available.
- For HUD placement also use `#panel-hud-layout-studio`: **Studio Apply** previews; **game Apply** saves. Verify the live region moves. Change shared layout machinery when the task calls for it, preserving working interactions and saved-layout compatibility.

## Commands and verification

Windows + PowerShell; forward slashes in code paths. Run commands from the applicable root or `game/` package.

- Development: `npm install`, `npm run dev`; **port 5173 only**. Check `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 5173` first. Reuse an existing server; never start a second or kill one to reclaim the port. `npm run lint` runs the conservative Biome baseline.
- Gameplay/data: relevant cages/tests and `npm run typecheck`; broaden checks when shared behavior changes. `npm run verify` runs all cages; `npm test` runs `game/tests/`.
- UI: typecheck, `npm --prefix game run check` (warnings fail), focused tests for changed behavior, `npm --prefix game run build` for the production bundle, and integrated-browser interaction/appearance checks for behavior/layout changes.
- Coverage (optional report): `npm --prefix game run test:coverage`; no threshold is enforced yet.
- Docs/comments only: inspect the edited files and local links; no gameplay suite or browser check.
- Wiki: `npm run wiki` when wiki source, displayed data/formulas or player-facing behavior changes. `docs/wiki/*.html` is generated; never hand-edit. UI-only changes do not trigger wiki rebuilds.
- Other generators: `npm run skills`, `npm run gallery`, or the relevant `tools/` entry point when its input changes.
- Verify correctness/compatibility, not prescribed balance or content counts. Do not gate pacing bands, prices, tuned windows, roster sizes or content quotas. Do not rerun passing checks without a relevant change or unresolved concern.

## Saves and workspace boundaries

- Migrations preserve counts, progress and meaning. Check old-save loading, migration and round-trip when saves change; reject unknown versions. Ask before lossy changes or breaking imports/exports/external consumers. Update all readers, writers and validators when changing data identities.
- Keep tree power out of `mob_HP`. One tab owns the exclusive Web Lock for writes; other tabs stay read-only until takeover. Without Web Locks, saving stays disabled.
- Do not commit or push unless explicitly asked. Commit messages use `<type: short summary>`. Establish the winning side before replace-all operations.
- Always pull with the hard-replace method: `git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/master`. This discards local tracked changes to match the remote.
- Finish when the requested behavior, affected layers and required checks agree. Review edited files and acceptance criteria directly, report changes/checks/blockers briefly, and stop.

# Map terrain artwork contract

The ground projection is owned by `game/src/ui/map/map-projection.ts`. Run `npm run map -- --write` to regenerate the map and the matching templates in `art-reference/map/geometry/`.

The portable [map art reference kit](../art-reference/map/README.md) contains shape references, role-labelled style references, camera and alignment calibration, agent briefs and prompts. Its refresh script derives geometry directly from the projection without rebuilding or modifying the live map.

## Full-hex artwork

Public map assets have three top-level folders: `terrain/` for natural ground/scenery and its `templates/`, `landmark/` for settlements, ruins, camps and event scenery, and `characters/` for figures. `characters/player/` holds the traveller; `characters/species/<species>/` holds that species' approved figures, with originals alongside numbered versions (`kobold.png`, `kobold-v2.png`). Generated candidates stay under `art-reference/` until approved, then copy into the matching species folder; do not mix raw, cutout or rejected files into public assets. Registration is selected by footprint metadata, not by a special directory name. The original-image coverage list is owned by `art-reference/map/source-assets.json`.

Use `hex-mask.png` or `hex-mask.svg` as the shape reference. Exact canvas-space vertices and projection matrix are in `terrain-hex.json` in the same folder; do not transcribe rounded coordinates into renderer code. The reference canvas is 1024 × 625, with its centre at (512, 312.5). It maps to the projected ground bounding rectangle, without alpha cropping or a second camera rotation. Artwork can have a different raster resolution when the same normalized footprint is retained.

The descriptive camera is orthographic, elevation 38° above ground and board yaw −16° in renderer coordinates. Upright vegetation must already depict that view. Keep it inside the footprint for terrain tiles; separate objects can extend above their ground footprint.

Those values are the artwork calibration and the runtime camera's default pose. `createMapProjection` also supplies the orbiting ground-plane projection. `game/src/ui/map/map-scene.ts` projects the coloured ground polygons, keeps each terrain diorama and actor upright with its inverse, and sorts scene cells by projected depth. The active catalogue uses one transparent diorama per hex, anchored by its painted bounds. Full-hex paintings and their registrations are retained outside the active catalogue. Orbiting a diorama does not generate unseen sides of its painted objects.

The terrain catalogue is `game/src/ui/map/map-terrain.ts`. Preserve originals and use numbered sibling assets (`forest-relief-1.png`, `forest-relief-2.png`, etc.). Selecting a replacement is an explicit catalogue change; filename numbering does not automatically activate it.

`TERRAIN_ART` selects the diorama a biome shows. `TERRAIN_VARIANTS` may list approved alternate dioramas; the map generator picks stably per hex. Each active diorama needs painted bounds in `game/src/ui/map/data/map-sprite-bounds.json`, and the biome's default is never repeated in its variant list. Full-hex assets require the separate footprint registration described below before intentional activation as ground artwork.

Settlements select their art through `LANDMARK_ART` in `tools/map.ts`, whose default town image comes from `TERRAIN_ART.town`. Full-hex landmark ground uses the same registration as terrain. A separate landmark diorama may omit its own tile base: the renderer places it over the coloured ground hex and aligns it using the painted-bounds anchor in `game/src/ui/map/data/map-sprite-bounds.json`. An optional seventh value scales a sprite slightly past its ground footprint to let roofs or walls cross into adjacent hexes. A landmark variant must be selected through `LANDMARK_ART` and have its asset/bounds available. M15 checks centring, bottom anchoring and the registered spill limit on settlement cells too.

Generated images may approximate the requested polygon. Measure the six ground vertices before activation with the measurement tool, which reads the tile's own silhouette and stores measured pixel coordinates, source dimensions and an opaque ground fill in `game/src/ui/map/data/map-terrain-footprints.json`:

```powershell
python tools/map-art.py /map/terrain/forest-relief-1.png
```

It takes the alpha ≥128 silhouette, reduces its convex hull to six corners and matches them against the template hex, so the stored order is the template's own. A recorded ground fill is kept, because the fill is a judgement about the picture; a new tile gets the median colour of the ground inside its own footprint. Re-measuring rewrites only the entries named on the command line.

The generator registers six triangular sectors sharing the measured footprint centre, mapping all six vertices exactly onto the projected hex. An outer ground clip and the ground fill prevent painted edge irregularities and antialias seams from leaving gaps. Because each sector maps its own pair of corners exactly, that fit cannot see a footprint recorded in the wrong rotational order: the generator therefore also measures the footprint against the template hex and refuses a footprint that sits more than 12% of the canvas away, which is the margin between an approximate tile and a mis-ordered one. Keep trees inside the footprint: this registration is for complete terrain tiles, not tall objects that intentionally extend beyond the ground.

Use the development-only **Hex alignment** checkbox under Map tools → Controls to compare the actual artwork with the projected ground outline and centre cross. M15 verifies placement metadata and generated markup, not painted-edge accuracy. Dioramas use painted-bounds anchoring rather than six-sector ground registration.

## Forest version 1 generation brief

Built-in image generation; shape reference: `art-reference/map/geometry/hex-mask.png`; style reference: the original `game/public/map/terrain/forest-relief.png`.

> One painterly fantasy tabletop forest tile. Match the shape reference's complete projected hex footprint and framing. Orthographic elevation 38°, board yaw −16°. Opaque moss/grass/earth to all six edges, transparent outside. Three small pine trees inside the central area with 8% clearance from the silhouette. Muted greens, top-left lighting. No platform thickness, outer shadow, border, path, buildings, characters or text. Preserve transparent alpha. Requested reference canvas: 1024 × 625; measure the actual output dimensions and footprint before placement.

**Tool Call: docs\glossary.md**
