# Glossary

Short definitions of game terms. Read only the terms needed for the task. Document ownership and update policy: [AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md#document-map).

# The 2 Layers of an Item

| Term           | Meaning                                                                                                        |
| -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Item level** | The level a piece dropped at — the one axis its Mod values ride.                                               |
| **Band**       | low · mid · high — the label the drop source's zone already carries.                                           |
| **Tier**       | Which third of a Mod's value window the roll landed in. One item carries one Tier set, shared by all its Mods. |

# Attack and Defend Layers

A **layer** is one step of the calculation, in a fixed order. A layer either **removes** the hit, **reduces** the damage, **scales** it, or **receives** it.

Two words that are constantly confused:

- **Offensive / Defensive** are **Mod pools** — which Mods may roll on which slot.
- **Attack layer / Defend layer** is the **runtime order** — what happens to one number, in sequence.

# Item and Mod Vocabulary

| Term             | Meaning                                                                                                                                                   |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Stat**         | A numeric value that measures or affects a character's or mob's capabilities; includes Core attributes and derived stats.                                 |
| **Mod**          | One rolled stat line on an item, read as `name value (Tier)`.                                                                                             |
| **Flat**         | A value added straight into the stat, before any % modifier runs.                                                                                         |
| **%**            | A multiplier applied to the finished stat.                                                                                                                |
| **Stat Mod**     | A Mod that is neither Offensive nor Defensive. It rolls one or all of the seven Core attributes, and it rolls on every item.                              |
| **Frame Mod**    | The first line of a dropped item — the frame's own line, rolled from the slot's Frame-Mod pool.                                                           |
| **Weapon type**  | The held weapon family that sets its attack tempo, damage multiplier, skill pool and bound skills.                                                        |
| **Weapon frame** | A named variant inside a weapon type. It fixes that drop's Frame Mod identity and carries its own drop weight and value bias.                             |
| **Bound Mod**    | The pair of lines after the Frame Mod, fixed at drop.                                                                                                     |
| **Unbound Mod**  | Every line past the Bound pair — the set the value stones, Add and Remove work on.                                                                        |
| **Gear Mod**     | A piece's own inherent defence value — Armour, Evasion or Energy Shield, decided by its Base school. It is shown on its own top line, inside no Mod list. |
| **Base**         | The frame of one slot (`Ring Mail` / `Plate Vest` / `Vestment`). It decides **weight** and which Mods are Primary or Secondary.                           |
| **Weight**       | What an item carries, from its Base, multiplied by quality. Not a rolled value.                                                                           |
| **Capacity**     | How much weight a build can carry, set by Str.                                                                                                            |
| **Level floor**  | The first level of a band — what an away window (offline) is limited to; the window above it is the band's own ceiling.                                   |

# Stats and Formulas

| Term                                             | Meaning                                                                                                                                                 |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Core attribute**                               | One of the seven foundational values: Str · Agi · Vit · Dex · Int · Wis · Lck.                                                                          |
| **Derived stat**                                 | A combat value calculated from Core attributes and other inputs such as level, gear or effects.                                                         |
| **K value**                                      | The hidden constant that converts a Core attribute into a game value — `K_STR` is physical power a point of Str.                                        |
| **Cap**                                          | An upper limit applied to a value.                                                                                                                      |
| **Alignment**                                    | Dex spent twice: the gate **every rolled status** passes — an Element status, bleed, and a stun — **and** the multiplier on an Element status's damage. |
| **Physical power / Magic power**                 | The damage derived from the character. There is no weapon Base power.                                                                                   |
| **Elemental power**                              | The third damage path, derived from Int and named by the weapon's own Element.                                                                          |
| **Current HP cost**                              | A flat HP amount paid by a skill from the caster's current pool; a press cannot spend its final HP point.                                               |
| **Caster Max HP damage**                         | The optional `max_hp_pct` term added to a skill's damage basis, read from the caster's Max HP.                                                          |
| **hit_chance**                                   | Whether a hit connects at all — the accuracy-versus-evasion ratio.                                                                                      |
| **crit overflow**                                | Chance past a whole chance becomes crit damage, so stacking more crit is never wasted.                                                                  |
| **damage taken**                                 | A multiplier on the incoming hit that runs after every mitigation layer and before any pool.                                                            |
| **global damage / global defend / global speed** | The three reserved umbrella multipliers (`engine.json` `global`).                                                                                       |

# Combat

| Term               | Meaning                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Push**           | HP reaching zero is **not death**: the fighter is pushed out of combat, rests, then walks back in alone. Time is the only thing this game charges. |
| **Camp**           | Short for Field Camp: a player-set safe hex that receives a Push and enables field gathering and cooking.                                          |
| **No death**       | The standing rule: defensive value comes from time not lost, not from survival.                                                                    |
| **DoT**            | Damage over time, ticking once a second.                                                                                                           |
| **Leech**          | HP returned as a percentage of damage just dealt.                                                                                                  |
| **Setup / payoff** | A setup row applies a status; a payoff row reads or spends that same status for its own effect.                                                    |
| **Status present** | An auto-cast leg that holds a payoff row until the target carries the status the row exploits; `statusStacksAtLeast` adds a stack floor.           |
| **Consume**        | Spending a status's stacks for extra damage. The press removes only the stacks it spends, after the hit.                                           |
| **Spread**         | Copying a live status line to another target. The copy keeps its stacks and remaining life and starts no new clock.                                |
| **Retired skill**  | A legacy row kept resolvable for old saves but excluded from drops, named rewards and the live roster.                                             |
| **Perfect dodge**  | Removes the hit outright, and it is not contested.                                                                                                 |
| **Reach**          | How far a build can act **in a fight**: near and far are a queue, not a range band.                                                                |
| **Foe**            | The **Field of Enemies** — every mob the character is fighting at once.                                                                            |
| **Elite**          | A flag on a Large body, never a size of its own: a rank over the rolled variant, keeping its name.                                                 |

# Field and HUD

| Term                  | Meaning                                                     |
| --------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Player Vital Card** | The player identity, vitals and combat-feedback component.  |
| **Commands dock**     | The HUD group for game speed and pause/resume controls.     |
| **Menu hub**          | The HUD group for navigation and field controls.            |
| **Objectives**        | The HUD feed for the run target and tracked Delivery wants. |

# Elements and Statuses

| Term                  | Meaning                                                                                                                                          |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Element**           | fire · cold · lightning · poison · chaos · earth. One item holds exactly one, and it decides which status the item can inflict.                  |
| **Innate element**    | The Element a normal or Elite mob inherits from its Species (`mob.species[].element`); a zone Boss may declare its own (`mob.bosses[].element`). |
| **burn** (fire)       | Damage over time.                                                                                                                                |
| **chill** (cold)      | A cut to the target's attack speed and Armour. No accuracy cut.                                                                                  |
| **shock** (lightning) | Cuts accuracy and stops the clock for 0.5 sec, under the control budget.                                                                         |
| **crippled** (earth)  | Cuts outgoing direct damage by 20%. No attack clock or cooldown cut.                                                                             |
| **stun**              | Not a status: a stop proc that reuses the shock stop.                                                                                            |
| **poison** (poison)   | Stacking damage over time.                                                                                                                       |
| **mark** (chaos)      | A growing multiplier on the hit it rides, plus leech.                                                                                            |
| **bleed**             | Physical damage over time. **Not an Element** — no Element tag and no resistance line.                                                           |

# The passive tree

| Term                  | Meaning                                                                                                                                                             |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Region**            | One of the tree's seven attribute areas — Str, Agi, Dex, Int, Wis, Vit, Lck. Each opens from Start and connects to neighbouring regions through the shared network. |
| **Node**              | One thing the tree grants: a Core attribute, a Notable profile, or a Keystone mechanic. Every node has one rank.                                                    |
| **Rank**              | One step of a node; a rank is bought at the node's own cost and the tree's current nodes each hold one.                                                             |
| **Normal**            | A node that grants exactly +1 of its region's Core attribute, for 1 tree point.                                                                                     |
| **Notable**           | A node that grants a profile of two or three flat / percent lines, for 3 tree points.                                                                               |
| **Junction**          | A Notable that bridges two neighbouring regions.                                                                                                                    |
| **Keystone**          | A node that changes a mechanic, for 1 attainment point. It is grantless unless its effect adds a stat, and it may be incompatible with another Keystone.            |
| **Incompatibility**   | A listed pair of Keystones that may not be held together. Exclusivity is pairwise only; there are no groups.                                                        |
| **Attainment point**  | The tree's second currency. A completed Delivery contract pays one; keystones are bought with them.                                                                 |
| **Tree point**        | The ordinary tree currency: a base plus the level curve, plus Town/Delivery quest bonuses, less what the ranks spent.                                               |
| **Quest tree bonus**  | An extra tree point stored in a Town task or Delivery offer at generation; it is paid once, when the reward is actually claimed.                                    |
| **Low Life**          | Current HP at or below half of **Full Max HP**. A reservation that lowers usable HP does not cause it; Chaos Inoculation is never Low Life.                         |
| **Full Max / usable** | Full Max is the pool before reservation; usable is what healing and spending may reach. Reservations lower usable only.                                             |

# Crafting

| Term                             | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Reroll**                       | Re-rolls the value inside a Mod, staying in the same Tier.                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **Roll new Mod**                 | Re-rolls a line's **identity**: the Mod is redrawn from the piece's own Base pool.                                                                                                                                             |
| **Polish**                       | One press over every line of a piece: each value re-rolls inside its own Tier.                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Refine**                       | Raises a Mod one Tier.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Ascend**                       | Raises Item quality one step for the whole item.                                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Remove stone**                 | Deletes one Unbound Mod.                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| **Add stone**                    | Fills one empty Unbound slot from the piece's own Base pool.                                                                                                                                                                   |
| **Replace stone**                | The chosen swap: the player names the Mod that comes in, drawn from the piece's own pool.                                                                                                                                      |
| **Imprint stone**                | Rewrites one Unbound line as the stone's own Mod, with a fresh roll from that Mod's window.                                                                                                                                    |
| **Quality stone**                | The only source of Gear Mod points.                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| **Tier stone**                   | Buys the tier presses.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Value stone**                  | A stone spent on rerolling Mod values.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Polish stone**                 | Buys Polish the piece.                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **Reforge stone**                | Buys Reforge the piece: the Tier redrawn across the whole piece.                                                                                                                                                               |
| **Rebirth stone**                | Buys Rebirth the Unbound lines — the set the piece holds, Add lines included.                                                                                                                                                  |
| **Corrupt stone / Repair stone** | Stones spent on the Corrupt and Repair presses.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| **Upgrade**                      | Adds Gear Mod points to a piece, one step at a time, with rising failure odds.                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Corrupt**                      | One gamble per piece: a roll that can take the piece somewhere better or ruin it.                                                                                                                                              |
| **Salvage**                      | Dismantling gear into base ore and Scrap; it does not directly mint a Value stone.                                                                                                                                             |
| **Scrap**                        | The material produced by Salvage and consumed by Alchemy to make Value stones.                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Alchemy**                      | A settlement recipe that immediately converts Scrap into Value stones and advances Alchemy-based Tier milestones.                                                                                                              |
| **Bag filter**                   | What makes every drop a decision: **keep** it, **dissolve** it, or **sell** it.                                                                                                                                                |
| **bag**                          | What the character carries: kept gear (one piece a slot) and carried consumable, field-material and junk stacks, all counted against one slot pool.                                                                            |
| **stash**                        | Settlement storage, organisation only.                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| **herb**                         | A gathered or farmed plant used for brewing/cooking or sold as a trade good.                                                                                                                                                   |
| **field material**               | A carried stack produced by Mine, Rare Grove, Smithing or hunting activity.                                                                                                                                                    |
| **Fishing**                      | A timed gathering activity at a Field Camp in a zone with an authored fishing source.                                                                                                                                          |
| **Smithing**                     | Settlement recipes that process ore and timber into metal or components; it does not craft gear.                                                                                                                               |
| **Forge**                        | A settlement service that turns one material into a chosen weapon or armour piece. The material's family picks the Base or weapon Frame; its grade sets the item band.                                                         |
| **Pattern**                      | One Forge output shape: an armour slot or a weapon type. Its material family and count come from `engine.json` `forge`.                                                                                                        |
| **Material grade**               | The 1–3 tier of a Forge material. It selects the item band and the character/smithing gates; higher grades need higher levels.                                                                                                 |
| **Material family**              | The Forge grouping that selects a Base school or weapon frame set: metal, wood, organic or essence.                                                                                                                            |
| **meal**                         | A cooked food item; eating one replaces the active timed combat buff.                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Hunger**                       | The character's food/provision meter.                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| **Auto Eat**                     | Automatic consumption of carried provisions to restore Hunger.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **provision**                    | Carried food or cooking ingredients.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| **trail event**                  | An independent travel-block event that finds the current zone's regional food or restores Hunger; it never replaces the block's ambush roll.                                                                                   |
| **trail site**                   | An authored optional map stop offering a one-time regional provision bundle, Hunger restoration or a survey of surrounding blocks.                                                                                             |
| **scouted block**                | A block whose landmark and encounter details have been learned by approaching it or surveying Hunting Tracks.                                                                                                                  |
| **explored block**               | A block the character has stood on; the map journal remembers it across saves.                                                                                                                                                 |
| **junk**                         | A flavoured drop from a **variant**, sold to the settlement Counterhand for gold.                                                                                                                                              |
| **trade good**                   | Carried junk, material, provision or farm herb that a town Counterhand buys; ingredients can instead be kept for their recipes and field uses.                                                                                 |
| **Demand**                       | A town's unfilled appetite for one goods category. Supplying it lowers that category's premium until demand recovers over game time.                                                                                           |
| **Supply**                       | The saved base value already delivered into a town's category demand pool; it is shared across items in that category.                                                                                                         |
| **Workshop**                     | A settlement service that consumes gathered materials to make finished trade goods and grants the recipe's field skill XP.                                                                                                     |
| **variant**                      | One named form of a Species (`mob.variants`): it owns a level band, authored Core allocation, may override the Species' default damage type, and selects its junk row. A Species may author any number of Variants.            |
| **unique**                       | A named wild boss belonging to a Species (`mob.uniques`): an optional rare upgrade of a normal spawn. A Species can have none or several.                                                                                      |
| **mob kit**                      | The optional list of mob skills one spawn resolves from `tools/data/mob-skills.json`, capped at 4. Resolution is an override, never a merge: Unique > Boss > Variant > Species. A Species without a kit keeps its basic swing. |
| **aura scope**                   | Where a mob aura applies: `engaged` affects the front three bodies of the group; `line` affects only bodies on the source's own formation line. Strongest wins and copies do not stack.                                        |

# Town and Economy

| Term                                  | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Settlement**                        | A named place holding services and NPCs, and the state the player is in while there.                                                                                         |
| **Adventure**                         | The other state: in a zone, fighting and looting.                                                                                                                            |
| **Capital**                           | A settlement serving one band with the full service set.                                                                                                                     |
| **Zone**                              | The combat area attached to a settlement.                                                                                                                                    |
| **Block**                             | One hex of the world lattice; a walk is counted in blocks.                                                                                                                   |
| **Walk**                              | Crossing blocks from the cell the feet are on to the cell clicked.                                                                                                           |
| **Waypoint**                          | A settlement opened by arriving on foot: after that a warp there is instant.                                                                                                 |
| **Forward**                           | Auto-walk to the next already-open settlement when the current zone's level band is behind; new settlements still need a first walk.                                         |
| **Patrol**                            | An optional walk-and-hunt circuit through named subzones in one visited zone.                                                                                                |
| **Expedition**                        | A Guild task targeting one Species' Elites in one subzone.                                                                                                                   |
| **Auto-Return**                       | Optional Patrol help that walks to town once the bag nears full, stashes unlocked pieces, and resumes the saved route when space was freed. It never sells or discards gear. |
| **Hunt**                              | Leaving safe ground to fight from the cell the feet stand on; sub-zones pick a cast, bare ground hunts the whole zone.                                                       |
| **Field Camp**                        | One player-set safe hex. It enables field gathering and cooking, and receives a Push in its zone.                                                                            |
| **Mine**                              | A wild-side fieldwork hex that yields ore while gathering at a Camp.                                                                                                         |
| **Rare Grove**                        | A wild-side fieldwork hex that yields timber and can yield rarewood while gathering at a Camp.                                                                               |
| **Dungeon run**                       | A **mode**, not a place: one dungeon per zone, entered at its wild-side index 0.                                                                                             |
| **Retreat**                           | Leaving a dungeon run with a subset of its escrow loot.                                                                                                                      |
| **Escrow**                            | What a dungeon run holds while it runs: the per-kill rolls banked instead of paid.                                                                                           |
| **Wild side**                         | The untamed cells on a settlement's own land.                                                                                                                                |
| **Standing**                          | A per-settlement tier earned from kills in that settlement's zone; it unlocks listed town services and Collector set turn-ins.                                               |
| **Gold**                              | The town-spending medium earned by selling trade goods and completing delivery wants.                                                                                        |
| **Haggling**                          | Town trading progression, separate from combat skills, Standing and life-skill Mastery.                                                                                      |
| **Delivery want / Delivery Contract** | A timed town request for a named good and quantity, with a completion reward.                                                                                                |
| **Track**                             | An informational reminder for an open Delivery want.                                                                                                                         |
| **Delivery clock**                    | The simulation clock used for Delivery deadlines.                                                                                                                            |
| **Delivery recap**                    | The saved outcome and proceeds of a Delivery want.                                                                                                                           |
| **Black Market**                      | The town stall selling rare goods and named Skill XP Levels for Gold.                                                                                                        |
| **Skill XP Level**                    | A combat skill's own XP-based level, distinct from the Duplicate Ladder and life-skill Mastery.                                                                              |
| **Collector set**                     | A named bundle of gear pieces a settlement wants handed in.                                                                                                                  |
| **Reservation**                       | An aura holding back a share of Max Mana.                                                                                                                                    |
| **reserve tier**                      | The share of the pool one aura holds back.                                                                                                                                   |

# Mobs

| Term             | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| ---------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Race**         | The broad fantasy grouping above Species (`mob.races`, assigned by `mob.species[].race`), such as Humanoid, Undead or Beast. Race membership is taxonomy and does not grant mechanics by itself. It is the single word used in data, code, cages and player text. |
| **Species**      | One individual creature lineage, such as Goblin, Orc or Golem (`mob.species`). A Species belongs to one Race and owns its gameplay data.                                                                                                                          |
| **body class**   | The four mob sizes — Small · Medium · Large · Boss (`mob.sizes`).                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| **Base school**  | The three armour families a Base belongs to: light (Evasion), heavy (Armour), cloth (Energy Shield).                                                                                                                                                              |
| **weapon group** | The three families a weapon belongs to: melee, ranged, magic.                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| **mob accuracy** | Derived from the mob's own stats through the same K values the player uses, scaled by the Species accuracy tier.                                                                                                                                                  |

# Abbreviations

| Term                 | Abbreviation |
| -------------------- | ------------ |
| Attack speed         | `aspd`       |
| Cooldown reduction   | `cdr`        |
| Critical chance      | `crit`       |
| Physical power       | `phys`       |
| Elemental power      | `elem`       |
| Damage per second    | `DPS`        |
| Elemental resistance | `res`        |
| Elemental alignment  | `align`      |
| Accuracy             | `acc`        |
| Evasion              | `ev`         |
| Energy Shield        | `ES`         |
| Max HP               | `HP`         |
| Max Mana             | `mp`         |
| Damage over time     | `DoT`        |
| Experience           | `XP`         |

# Skill: lean-agent

# Lean Agent

Task guidance for simplifying repository work. Not a persistent voice. User intent and `AGENTS.md` take precedence; tool, verification and scope policy live there — point to it rather than restating it.

## Priorities

1. Correctness, behavior, data, security and accessibility before effort or code size.
2. Complete the requested scope. Never ship a reduced version and ask afterward whether the full task was wanted.
3. Simplify only when the result stays clear, maintainable and equivalent.

## Loop

1. **Understand** — read the relevant source, docs and callers; state the expected behavior.
2. **Find the cause** — trace shared behavior; fix it once at its source, not at each symptom.
3. **Change the least** — reuse existing code and platform features; no speculative abstractions, dependencies or scaffolding.
4. **Check narrowly** — run the focused check for the changed behavior first, then follow the verification scope in `AGENTS.md`; broaden when a shared contract changed.
5. **Stop** — when acceptance criteria pass. Do not refactor adjacent code, and do not repeat passing checks without a relevant change.

## Do not cut

A shortcut is valid only when it cannot produce a wrong, lossy or insecure result. Even under time pressure, keep:

- Validation and error handling at system boundaries (user input, external data, files, saves).
- Save and migration compatibility, including old-save load and round-trip.
- Every check `AGENTS.md` requires; never skip verification to save effort.
- Accessibility semantics and keyboard access.

Drop instead: defensive handling for inputs internal code already guarantees.

## Communication

- Lead with the result: what changed, exact identifiers and numbers, caveats, evidence.
- Fuller explanation for documentation, reports and complex work, or when the user asks.
- Finish the authorized task before suggesting optional additions; ask only when a missing decision blocks correct work.

## Illustrative example

Task: "fix a duplicate-drop bug in the loot roll."

- **Lean-correct:** read the roll, find the shared `rng` consumed twice, fix that one ordering, run the loot cage.
- **Over-lean:** rewrite the roll API and re-run the whole suite "while here."
- **Wrong minimalism:** delete the boundary validation that rejects a malformed drop so the failing test passes.

import { BASES } from '../../../engine/client';
import type { ArenaCharacterArt, ArenaSpriteFrameImage, ArenaSpriteSheet } from './arena-art';
import { arenaScreenAngleFor } from '../../../presentation/arena-camera';
import equipment from './player-equipment-v1.json';
import type { Character } from '../../../sim/core/player';
import type { GameState, Item } from '../../../sim/core/types';

type Point = { x: number; y: number };
type Bounds = [number, number, number, number];
type EquipmentView = {
href: string;
imageWidth: number;
imageHeight: number;
rawAlphaBounds: Bounds | null;
visibleBoundsAlphaGt8: Bounds;
pivotSource: Point;
forwardAxisSource: Point;
pivotProvenance: string;
tolerancePx: number;
};
type EquipmentRecord = {
targetLengthBodyHeightRatio: number;
attachmentHand: 'main' | 'offhand';
views: Record<string, EquipmentView>;
};
type EquipmentFrame = ArenaSpriteFrameImage;

const source = equipment as unknown as {
schemaVersion: number;
frameCanvas: { width: number; height: number; anchor: Point };
body: Record<string, Record<string, EquipmentFrame[]>>;
weapons: Record<string, EquipmentRecord>;
shield: { targetHeightBodyHeightRatio: number; attachmentHand: 'off'; views: Record<string, EquipmentView> };
bodySkillOverrides?: Record<string, Partial<Record<'east' | 'west', EquipmentFrame>>>;
};

function sheet(frames: readonly EquipmentFrame[], frameMs: number, loop: boolean, impactMs?: number, release = false): ArenaSpriteSheet {
const first = frames[0];
const releaseGrip = release ? frames[1]?.mainGripCell ?? first.mainGripCell : undefined;
return {
href: first.href,
frameWidth: source.frameCanvas.width,
frameHeight: source.frameCanvas.height,
imageWidth: first.imageWidth,
imageHeight: first.imageHeight,
sourceFrames: frames.map(frame => frame.sourceFrame),
frameImages: frames,
columns: 1,
rows: 1,
frames: frames.length,
frameMs,
loop,
...(impactMs == null ? {} : { impactMs }),
...(releaseGrip ? { releaseSocket: { ...releaseGrip, provenance: 'authored-fallback' as const } } : {}),
};
}

const idle = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(source.body.idle).map(([direction, frames]) => [direction, sheet(frames, 140, true)]));
const walk = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(source.body.walk).map(([direction, frames]) => [direction, sheet(frames, 130, true)]));
const attack = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(source.body.attack).map(([direction, frames]) => [direction, sheet(frames, 100, false, 100, true)]));
const hit = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(source.body.hit).map(([direction, frames]) => [direction, sheet(frames, 110, false)]));
const death = Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(source.body.death).map(([direction, frames]) => [direction, sheet(frames, 180, false)]));

/** Clean player body animation. Weapon and offhand pictures are drawn as independent layers. */
export const equippedPlayerArt: ArenaCharacterArt = {
pixelArt: true,
displayHeight: 240,
anchor: {
x: source.frameCanvas.anchor.x / source.frameCanvas.width,
y: source.frameCanvas.anchor.y / source.frameCanvas.height,
},
clips: { idle, walk, attack, hit, death } as ArenaCharacterArt['clips'],
};

/** Skill-specific contact artwork is used only when its baked equipment matches the worn set. */
export function playerSkillContactPose(state: GameState, character: Character, skillId: string, direction: string) {
const mainHand = state.gear.find((item): item is Item => !!item && !item.broken && item.slot === 'main hand');
const offhand = state.gear.find((item): item is Item => !!item && !item.broken && item.slot === 'off hand');
const type = weaponTypeOf(mainHand?.base ?? character.weaponName);
if (skillId !== 'attack.shield_bash' || type?.id !== 'one-handed sword' || !offhand || baseRow(offhand.base)?.family !== 'Shield')
return undefined;
return source.bodySkillOverrides?.[skillId]?.[direction.includes('west') ? 'west' : 'east'];
}

export type ArenaEquipmentLayer = {
href: string;
imageWidth: number;
imageHeight: number;
clipBounds: Bounds;
transform: string;
kind: 'weapon' | 'shield';
};

function baseRow(base: string) {
return (BASES.bases as { name: string; family?: string | null }[]).find(row => row.name === base);
}

/** Resolve the exact canonical frame name to its weapon family without guessing from melee/ranged group. */
function weaponTypeOf(base: string): { id: string; hands: string } | undefined {
const weapons = BASES.weapons as { name: string; hands?: string }[];
const direct = weapons.find(weapon => weapon.name === base);
if (direct) return { id: direct.name, hands: direct.hands ?? 'Single' };
for (const [id, frames] of Object.entries(BASES.weapon_frames as Record<string, { name: string }[]>)) {
if (frames.some(frame => frame.name === base))
return { id, hands: weapons.find(weapon => weapon.name === id)?.hands ?? 'Single' };
}
return undefined;
}

function itemView(view: EquipmentView, grip: Point, bodyHeight: number, desiredLength: number, facing: number): ArenaEquipmentLayer {
const [left, top, right, bottom] = view.visibleBoundsAlphaGt8;
const width = right - left, height = bottom - top;
const axis = view.forwardAxisSource;
const along = Math.max(1, width * Math.abs(axis.x) + height * Math.abs(axis.y));
const scale = bodyHeight * desiredLength / along;
const screenFacing = arenaScreenAngleFor({ x: Math.cos(facing), y: Math.sin(facing) });
const eastReference = arenaScreenAngleFor({ x: 1, y: 0 });
const rotation = (screenFacing - eastReference) * 180 / Math.PI;
const transform = `translate(${grip.x} ${grip.y}) rotate(${rotation}) scale(${scale}) translate(${-view.pivotSource.x} ${-view.pivotSource.y})`;
return { href: view.href, imageWidth: view.imageWidth, imageHeight: view.imageHeight,
clipBounds: view.visibleBoundsAlphaGt8, transform, kind: 'weapon' };
}

function shieldView(view: EquipmentView, grip: Point, bodyHeight: number, desiredHeight: number): ArenaEquipmentLayer {
const [, top, , bottom] = view.visibleBoundsAlphaGt8;
const scale = bodyHeight * desiredHeight / Math.max(1, bottom - top);
return {
href: view.href,
imageWidth: view.imageWidth,
imageHeight: view.imageHeight,
clipBounds: view.visibleBoundsAlphaGt8,
transform: `translate(${grip.x} ${grip.y}) scale(${scale}) translate(${-view.pivotSource.x} ${-view.pivotSource.y})`,
kind: 'shield',
};
}

/** Build equipment layers at the current actor's measured main/offhand cell sockets. */
export function playerEquipmentLayers(args: {
state: GameState;
character: Character;
frame?: EquipmentFrame;
bodyHeight: number;
clip: string;
phase?: string;
facing: number;
}): ArenaEquipmentLayer[] {
const { state, character, frame, bodyHeight, clip, phase, facing } = args;
if (!frame || !(bodyHeight > 0)) return [];
const mainHand = state.gear.find((item): item is Item => !!item && !item.broken && item.slot === 'main hand');
const base = mainHand?.base ?? character.weaponName;
const weaponType = weaponTypeOf(base);
const record = weaponType ? source.weapons[weaponType.id] : undefined;
const layers: ArenaEquipmentLayer[] = [];
const phaseKey = clip === 'attack'
? phase === 'windup' ? 'raised'
: phase === 'contact' || phase === 'active' ? 'foreshortened'
: 'side'
: 'side';
const isRanged = weaponType?.id === 'bow' || weaponType?.id === 'crossbow';
const selectedView = isRanged
? clip === 'attack' && phase === 'windup' ? 'drawn'
: clip === 'attack' && (phase === 'contact' || phase === 'active') ? 'released'
: 'ready'
: phaseKey;

const mainGrip = frame.mainGripCell;
if (record && mainGrip) {
const view = record.views[selectedView] ?? record.views.side ?? record.views.ready;
if (view) layers.push(itemView(view, mainGrip, bodyHeight, record.targetLengthBodyHeightRatio, facing));
}

const offhand = state.gear.find((item): item is Item => !!item && !item.broken && item.slot === 'off hand');
const offhandFamily = offhand ? baseRow(offhand.base)?.family : undefined;
const offGrip = frame.offGripCell;
if (offhandFamily === 'Shield' && offGrip) {
const stow = weaponType?.hands === 'Two' || weaponType?.hands === 'Two (range)';
const view = source.shield.views[stow ? 'stowed' : 'front'] ?? source.shield.views.front;
if (view) {
const sign = Math.cos(facing) < 0 ? -1 : 1;
const grip = stow ? { x: offGrip.x - sign * bodyHeight * .18, y: offGrip.y - bodyHeight * .35 } : offGrip;
layers.push(shieldView(view, grip, bodyHeight, source.shield.targetHeightBodyHeightRatio));
}
}
return layers;
}

import { pixelArenaArt } from './arena-art-pixel-v2';
import { beetleVariants } from './arena-art-beetle';

export type ArenaDirection =
| 'south' | 'east' | 'north' | 'west'
| 'south-east' | 'north-east' | 'north-west' | 'south-west';

export type ArenaSourceFrame = { x: number; y: number; width: number; height: number; offsetX: number; offsetY: number };

/** A standalone transparent pose PNG with its own source rectangle and untrimmed-cell sockets. _/
export type ArenaSpriteFrameImage = {
href: string;
imageWidth: number;
imageHeight: number;
sourceFrame: ArenaSourceFrame;
mainGripCell?: { x: number; y: number };
offGripCell?: { x: number; y: number };
/_* This source pose includes its weapon/offhand pixels; suppress separate equipment layers. */
equipmentBaked?: boolean;
};

export type ArenaSpriteSheet = {
href: string;
frameWidth: number;
frameHeight: number;
imageWidth?: number;
imageHeight?: number;
sourceFrames?: readonly ArenaSourceFrame[];
/** Optional one-PNG-per-frame source. Existing atlases continue to use `href` + `sourceFrames`. _/
frameImages?: readonly ArenaSpriteFrameImage[];
columns: number;
rows: number;
frames: number;
startFrame?: number;
anchor?: { x: number; y: number };
frameMs: number;
loop: boolean;
impactMs?: number;
/_* Hand/muzzle in the untrimmed cell at the release marker, not atlas coordinates. _/
releaseSocket?: { x: number; y: number; provenance: 'measured' | 'authored-fallback' };
/_* A one-sided sheet may be mirrored by the renderer instead of duplicating its frames. */
mirror?: boolean;
};

export type ArenaCharacterArt = {
displayHeight: number;
anchor: { x: number; y: number };
pixelArt?: boolean;
clips: Record<'idle' | 'walk' | 'attack', Partial<Record<ArenaDirection, ArenaSpriteSheet>>>
& Partial<Record<'hit' | 'death', Partial<Record<ArenaDirection, ArenaSpriteSheet>>>>;
};

export type ArenaPixelSpriteSet = {
hero: ArenaCharacterArt;
species: Readonly<Partial<Record<string, ArenaCharacterArt>>>;
};

export type ArenaArt = ArenaPixelSpriteSet & {
background: { href: string; width: number; height: number };
};

/** Pixel-v2 atlas set approved for the arena runtime; the painted ground remains until its later refresh. */
export const arenaArt: ArenaArt = {
background: { href: '/combat/arpg/forest-clearing.png', width: 1672, height: 941 },
hero: pixelArenaArt.hero,
species: pixelArenaArt.species,
};

/** Sprite art is selected by canonical species id; other actors retain their current art until converted. */
export function arenaArtForSpecies(speciesId: string | undefined, variant?: string): ArenaCharacterArt | null {
if (speciesId === 'beetle' && variant && beetleVariants[variant]) return beetleVariants[variant];
return speciesId ? arenaArt.species[speciesId] ?? null : null;
}

import type { ArenaCharacterArt, ArenaSpriteSheet, ArenaPixelSpriteSet } from './arena-art';

export type SpriteAtlasMetadata = {
sourceCanvas: { width: number; height: number };
frameCanvas: { width: number; height: number };
anchor: { x: number; y: number };
sourceFrames?: NonNullable<ArenaSpriteSheet['sourceFrames']>;
sourceFrameOrder?: number[];
frameBottoms?: number[];
releaseSockets?: Partial<Record<'east' | 'west', { x: number; y: number; provenance: string }>>;
};

export function pilotArt(href: string, atlas: SpriteAtlasMetadata, displayHeight: number, hoverAtRest = false): ArenaCharacterArt {
const socketFor = (direction: 'east' | 'west'): ArenaSpriteSheet['releaseSocket'] => {
const socket = atlas.releaseSockets?.[direction];
if (!socket) return undefined;
if (!Number.isFinite(socket.x) || !Number.isFinite(socket.y) || socket.x < 0 || socket.y < 0
|| socket.x > atlas.frameCanvas.width || socket.y > atlas.frameCanvas.height
|| !['measured', 'authored-fallback'].includes(socket.provenance))
throw new Error(`Invalid release socket: ${href} ${direction}`);
return { ...socket, provenance: socket.provenance === 'measured' ? 'measured' : 'authored-fallback' };
};
const sourceFrames = atlas.sourceFrames ?? Array.from({ length: 40 }, (_, index) => {
const sourceIndex = atlas.sourceFrameOrder?.[index] ?? index;
const bottom = atlas.frameBottoms?.[sourceIndex] ?? atlas.frameCanvas.height - 1;
return {
x: sourceIndex % 8 * atlas.frameCanvas.width,
y: Math.floor(sourceIndex / 8) * atlas.frameCanvas.height,
width: atlas.frameCanvas.width,
height: bottom + 1,
offsetX: 0,
offsetY: atlas.frameCanvas.height - 1 - bottom,
};
});
const sheet = (startFrame: number, frames = 4, frameMs = 140, loop = true): ArenaSpriteSheet => ({
href, frameWidth: atlas.frameCanvas.width, frameHeight: atlas.frameCanvas.height,
imageWidth: atlas.sourceCanvas.width, imageHeight: atlas.sourceCanvas.height, sourceFrames,
columns: 8, rows: 5, startFrame, frames, frameMs, loop,
});
return {
pixelArt: true,
displayHeight,
anchor: { x: atlas.anchor.x / atlas.frameCanvas.width, y: atlas.anchor.y / atlas.frameCanvas.height },
clips: {
idle: {
south: sheet(0, 1), 'south-east': sheet(1, 1), east: hoverAtRest ? sheet(8) : sheet(2, 1), 'north-east': sheet(3, 1),
north: sheet(4, 1), 'north-west': sheet(5, 1), west: hoverAtRest ? sheet(12) : sheet(6, 1), 'south-west': sheet(7, 1),
},
walk: { east: sheet(8), west: sheet(12) },
attack: {
east: { ...sheet(16, 4, 100, false), impactMs: 200, releaseSocket: socketFor('east') },
west: { ...sheet(20, 4, 100, false), impactMs: 200, releaseSocket: socketFor('west') },
},
hit: { east: sheet(24, 4, 65, false), west: sheet(28, 4, 65, false) },
death: { east: sheet(32, 4, 140, false), west: sheet(36, 4, 140, false) },
},
};

    // Tight-crop sheets index one authored rect per frame; an overrun must clamp to that list, never
    // fall back to a cell crop that would pull neighbouring frames into view.
    const sourceFrameCount = standaloneFrame ? sheet?.frameImages?.length ?? 0 : sheet?.sourceFrames?.length ?? 0;
    const sourceFrame = sourceFrameCount
      ? containedFrame(sheet, Math.min(frameIndex, sourceFrameCount - 1), standaloneFrame)
      : undefined;
    // Generated attack poses can fill much more of the fixed canvas than the idle sprite.
    // Normalize their visible body height against this direction's idle pose, pivoting at the feet.
    const bodyScale = actor.id === 'player' && art?.pixelArt && clipName === 'attack' && restFrame?.height && sourceFrame?.height
      ? restFrame.height / sourceFrame.height : 1;
    const equipmentLayers: ArenaEquipmentLayer[] = actor.id === 'player' && standaloneFrame && !standaloneFrame.equipmentBaked
      ? playerEquipmentLayers({ state: s, character: c, frame: standaloneFrame,
        bodyHeight: restFrame?.height ?? 0, clip: clipName, phase: pose?.phase, facing: actor.facing })
      : [];
    const skillEffects = actorSkillEffects(actor, dead);
    return { actor, ground, action, art, sheet, standaloneFrame, equipmentLayers, anchor, fallback, height, width, bodyScale,
      bodyHeight: restFrame ? restFrame.height * (pixelScale ?? height / (sheet?.frameHeight ?? 1)) : height,
      nameplateHeight, hitboxWidth, age, cue, statuses, clipName, sourceFrame, mirror: Boolean(sheet?.mirror), ...skillEffects,
      frame: sourceFrame && sheet ? `0 0 ${sheet.frameWidth} ${sheet.frameHeight}`
        : sheet ? arenaSpriteFrame(sheet, elapsedMs, reducedMotion, clipName === 'death') : '',
      x: art?.pixelArt ? Math.round(ground.x / ARENA_VIEW.width * stage.width) : ground.x / ARENA_VIEW.width * stage.width,
      y: art?.pixelArt ? Math.round(ground.y * scale) : ground.y * scale,
      bodyX: art?.pixelArt ? Math.round(Math.cos(angle) * reach * scale) : Math.cos(angle) * reach * scale,
      bodyY: art?.pixelArt ? Math.round(Math.sin(angle) * reach * scale) : Math.sin(angle) * reach * scale,
      brightness: hit && hitElapsedMs < 160 ? 1.6 : 1,
      opacity: actor.diedAtUs == null || actor.id === 'player' ? 1 : Math.max(0, 1 - age / 1.7),
      deadRotation: actor.diedAtUs == null || deathSheet || reducedMotion ? 0
        : Math.min(1, age / .32) * (Math.cos(arenaScreenAngleFor({ x: Math.cos(actor.facing), y: Math.sin(actor.facing) })) < 0 ? -78 : 78),
      shadow: actor.mob ? actorProfile(actor.mob).boss ? 47 : 29 : 23,
    };

}

function actionStyle(action: CombatArenaAction, mob?: Mob) {
if (mob) {
const skill = action.skillId ? mobSkillById(action.skillId) : null;
return arenaMobShape(skill, mob);
}

# ModWorld — 2.5D 3/4 pixel art และ VFX production plan

วันที่: 2026-10-27  
สถานะ: ทิศทางภาพ 2.5D pixel ล็อกแล้ว; งานทั้งหมดเป็น sprite/atlas 2D ที่ใช้ arena projection เดิม

**แผนนี้เป็นงาน 2.5D pixel art**: ตัวละคร อุปกรณ์ mob และ VFX เป็นภาพ pixel ที่วาด/เจนเป็น sprite และ atlas 2D แล้วประกอบบน ground plane ด้วย projection เดิมของ arena. ไม่มี geometry, rig, mesh หรือ renderer ใหม่ใน runtime; ภาพ concept และ sprite sheet เป็น deliverable ของงานนี้. ห้ามเริ่มผลิตทั้ง roster ก่อน proof ผ่าน.

**เมื่อ replacement ผ่าน QA และใช้งานร่วมกับ runtime ได้ ให้ integrator เปิดใช้เป็น default ของส่วนนั้นทันที ไม่ต้องรอทั้ง roster หรือขออนุมัติรายชิ้นซ้ำ**. ระบบเดิมที่ยังไม่ถูกแทนยังทำงานต่อ; ห้ามลบหรือทำให้ fallback เสีย.

## 1. Visual direction และ proof

### ภาพและสไตล์ที่ผู้ใช้เลือก

[ภาพนักธนูที่อนุมัติเป็น style reference](../../art-reference/players/pixel-archer-direction-concept-2026-10-27.png) ล็อกงาน pixel art รายละเอียดระดับภาพนี้: เส้นผม ผ้า หนัง อุปกรณ์ และ shading ที่มีมิติ; สัดส่วน chibi เล็กน้อย ใบหน้าแสดงอารมณ์และ silhouette ชัด ไม่บังคับลดรายละเอียดให้ pixel หยาบขึ้น ตรวจความอ่านออกที่ขนาดเล่นจริง

[Minotaur ที่มีอยู่](../../art-reference/monsters/minotaur/animation/source/base.png) เป็น reference ของ mob รูปร่างกะทัดรัด แข็งแรง ใบหน้าและอาวุธอ่านชัด รักษาสัดส่วน บุคลิก และความน่าเกรงขามเฉพาะของ mob แต่ละชนิด ให้ player และ mob อยู่ในโลกภาพเดียวกัน ไม่ทำทุกตัวเป็นของเล่นหน้าตาเหมือนกัน หลีกเลี่ยงตัวละครกล่อง voxel, ภาพมันวาว และภาพเบลอแทน pixel

ภาพนักธนูเป็น first-party concept สำหรับสไตล์; ชุดและสีเป็นตัวอย่าง ไม่ใช่เครื่องแบบของทุกตัวละคร

### โลก กล้อง และ gameplay

โลกเป็น 2.5D: ground plane หน่วยเมตร + sprite ที่มีความสูงเป็นภาพ; กล้อง 3/4 คงที่ตาม player ไม่ตาม target. ใช้ projection ของแต่ละ domain ตามของเดิม — arena ใช้ matrix จาก `ARENA_*` ใน `game/src/presentation/arena-camera.ts` และ map ใช้ `createMapProjection` (elevation 38°, yaw −16°) ใน `game/src/ui/map/map-projection.ts`; ห้ามสร้างกล้องใหม่หรือเปลี่ยน projection เพื่อให้ภาพง่ายขึ้น

Actor ใช้ 8 world directions ตาม `ARENA_DIRECTIONS`; baked sprite มี anchor/effect-socket/visible bounds ชัด (socket สำหรับ effect release/contact เท่านั้น ไม่ใช่จุดแปะอาวุธ); body footprint 0.5 m diameter; field 50 m. Gameplay timing, committed geometry และ actual receipts ยังเป็น authority; ภาพไม่เพิ่ม hit, timer, proc, reward หรือ RNG.

### ลำดับงานภาพที่ล็อก

1. **Character:** ผลิต sprite/animation ของตัวละครผู้เล่นทั้งหมดแบบ weapon-baked (body + weapon/offhand อยู่ใน pixels เดียวกันทุกเฟรม ไม่มี separate weapon atlas/layer animate) เริ่มจาก archer เป็นตัวแทน pipeline; ทุก class ใช้ pose matrix เดียวกันที่ proof ล็อก; version ที่ผ่าน QA เปิด default ทันที
2. **Mob:** ผลิต sprite/animation ของ mob ทั้ง roster แบบ weapon-baked เช่นกัน (อาวุธผูกติดกับ mob มาตั้งแต่ source pixels) เริ่มจาก minotaur เป็นตัวแทน; ทุก species/variant ใช้ pose matrix เดียวกับ player ต่างกันแค่ silhouette/บุคลิก/ขนาด; รักษาความน่าเกรงขามเฉพาะของแต่ละ species
3. **Skill VFX:** ผลิต/ปรับ authored pixel VFX ครบตาม live roster และ basic/mob paths โดยอิง `game/public/fx/skill-pool/vfx-production.md`; ใช้ canonical action/area/timing
4. **Map / terrain / environment:** ทำเป็นลำดับสุดท้าย คงของปัจจุบันไว้ระหว่างทาง; ใช้ terrain slice จริง 1–2 hex ใน proof เพื่อ calibrate scale

Phase 1 ปล่อยเป็น slice: proof → 1 actor + 1 mob → ต่อ class/family; ห้ามเริ่ม batch ถัดไปก่อน slice ก่อนหน้าผ่าน checklist/capture/budget.

### Proof ก่อนยกเครื่องทั้งเกม

1. ทำ archer พร้อม bow แบบ baked (bow อยู่ในมือทุกเฟรมตั้งแต่ draw → release), mob ตัวแทนแบบ weapon-baked, และ terrain slice จริง 1–2 hex พร้อมความสูง 0–2 ระดับ ในสไตล์ที่เลือก ให้เห็น idle → draw → release → flight → contact
2. ใช้ `attack.piercing_shot`: ลูกศรหนึ่งดอกตามแนวที่ commit ความยาว 5.2 m และ full width 0.75 m ตาม `tools/data/skills.json`; contact เฉพาะ recipient จริง ไม่ใช้ beam เต็มเส้นหรือลูกศรหลายดอกแทน hit เพิ่ม
3. Proof set ต้องมี: Piercing Shot, Cleave (sector 120°), persistent field 1 ตัว, aura 1 ตัว, channel/mobile effect 1 ตัว และ overlap scene ที่มี 2–3 effect พร้อม mob หลายตัว; ทดสอบที่ 8 world directions และมุมกลางระหว่าง bin
4. ตรวจใน browser ที่ 1920 × 1080 ด้วย arena camera matrix: alignment, height/depth, footprint, readability, reduced motion และ pixel stability (ไม่มี shimmer/crawl เกิน 1 native pixel)
5. วัดและบันทึก frame time p50/p95, heap, และ native resolution/upscale; production gate คือ 60 Hz floor (p95 16.8 ms, owner-accepted 2026-10-27) และห้ามใช้ dev showcase ที่มี debug overhead เป็นหลักฐาน
6. **ล็อก native resolution และ upscale factor** ใน decision record หลัง proof; เปลี่ยนค่าหลังล็อก = re-run proof
7. ถ้า proof ไม่ผ่าน budget ใช้ degraded tiers: ลด decorative density/quality → ลด directions ของ ambient/decor → ลด component ที่ไม่ใช่ cue หลัก → คง fallback เดิมของส่วนนั้น; ห้ามลดพื้นที่ cue หลักหรือเปลี่ยน gameplay shape

## 2. ขอบเขตและ ownership

- Canonical gameplay, skill identity และ save identity คงเดิม; presentation ไม่สร้าง damage, hits, timers หรือ RNG. งาน engine/runtime ใช้ [engine implementation plan](engine-implementation-work.md) เป็น contract
- **Image/2D asset generation เป็นของ art owner:** agent ไม่เจนภาพหรือแก้ asset; agent ตรวจ validator/tests/integration และหยุด/report ถ้า asset ขาด
- Art owner ส่ง source/candidate, provenance, native scale, anchor/socket, animation metadata, budgets และวิธี reproduce; integrator ผูก runtime และเลือก candidate ที่ผ่าน
- ใช้ first-party art; ไม่เพิ่ม third-party asset packs หรือ external generation services. งานภาพทุกชิ้นต้องมี provenance และ version
- Runtime renderer, camera และ projection เดิมเป็น authority; งานนี้ไม่เพิ่ม renderer/dependency ใหม่

### Versioned asset pool

- จัดงานแยกตาม subject/component และเก็บ candidate ใน `v1/`, `v2/`; player, mob, equipment, skill และ map มี identity/version ของตัวเอง
- Source/candidate อยู่ใต้ `art-reference/` ตาม subject; runtime อยู่ใต้ `game/src/ui/combat/arena/` สำหรับ actor art และ `game/public/fx/skill-pool/<skill-slug>/vN/` สำหรับ skill VFX; ห้ามใช้ path เดิมทับ version ที่ส่งแล้ว
- ใช้ lowercase hyphens; skill ใช้ slug เดิม เช่น `attack-piercing-shot`; 2D atlas metadata/QA ใช้ `game/public/fx/skill-pool/vfx-production.md` และ `tools/check-authored-vfx.py`
- Candidate ใหม่สร้าง version ใหม่; ระบุสถานะ `draft | candidate | accepted | selected | retired`; แยก review จาก default selection
- Integrator เปิด selected version เป็น default ราย slice; เก็บ version เดิมเป็น fallback; art version ไม่เปลี่ยน skill/save identity

## 3. Asset brief ก่อนผลิตแต่ละ component

ระบุ canonical skill/component, gameplay shape/origin/delivery/timestamps, actor/baked-set reference (body + weapon/offhand หนึ่งชุดต่อ loadout หรือ species-variant), camera/native resolution, footprint, pose matrix (actions × directions × frames ตามที่ proof ล็อก), frame grid, anchor/effect-socket, animation states, depth order (single sprite layer), reduced-motion variant, budget (texture size, frames, file size), provenance และ rejection criteria. Particle distribution ตามพื้นที่ ไม่ใช่จำนวน target; แยก component ตาม phase/motion/path. ห้าม brief แบบ body เปล่า + weapon ลอยมาประกบทีหลัง

## 4. 2.5D production contract

- Sprite/atlas ต้องอ่าน silhouette, pixel clusters, materials และ luminous core ได้ที่ขนาดเล่นจริง; การลด resolution อย่างเดียวไม่รับประกันคุณภาพ
- Cone/line/projectile/field แสดง full footprint/trajectory ตาม committed area; empty ground ต้องเห็น; hit เกิดตาม receipt จริง
- Pose matrix เทียบเท่าทุก character: proof ล็อก actions × directions × frames หนึ่งชุด (เช่น idle/walk/attack windup-contact-follow-through-recovery/hit/death/skill) แล้ว player ทุก class และ mob ทุก species/variant ใช้ matrix เดียวกัน ห้ามมีตัวที่ใช้ east/west-only แล้วให้ตัวอื่นใช้เต็ม หรือแชร์ body ข้าม weapon family; วาด native ต่อ 8 world directions สำหรับ 2.5D 3/4 ไม่หมุน side view แทนทิศอื่น
- ทุกเฟรมเป็น baked pixel sprite 2.5D 3/4 (body + weapon/offhand ใน pixels เดียวกัน วาด foreshorten/raised/side ตามทิศนั้น ๆ); anchor/visible bounds อ้างกับ baked cell เดียว; socket มีเฉพาะ effect release/contact ไม่ใช่จุดแปะอาวุธ; ห้าม separate weapon PNG, grip/pivot estimate, หรือ rotate/scale อาวุธแยกชั้นตอน runtime; depth order ตาม ground plane; ห้ามฝัง actor ใน effect ที่ต้องแยก
- One-shot/pulse/loop/exit/interruption ตรง lifecycle จริง; decoration ไม่เพิ่ม hit หรือบดบังพื้นที่สำคัญ; fallback ทำงานเมื่อ candidate ผิด/ไม่ผ่าน
- Reduced motion ยังคงพื้นที่และ cue สำคัญ; ไม่มี shimmer/crawl เกิน 1 native pixel
- Reject: body เปล่า + weapon ลอย, grip/pivot estimate แทน baked pixels, แชร์ body ข้าม weapon family, action มีไม่ครบทุกทิศตาม pose matrix ที่ proof ล็อก
- `equipment-v1` แบบแยกชั้น (body + weapon PNG หมุนแปะตอน runtime) อยู่ต่อเฉพาะเป็น fallback; งานใหม่ทุก slice เป็น baked set และเปิด default แทนเมื่อผ่าน QA

## 5. Skill VFX contracts

รายละเอียดราย skill และ QA อยู่ที่ [authored VFX production](../../game/public/fx/skill-pool/vfx-production.md) และ atlas ต่อ skill; ตารางนี้เป็น contract ระดับ family:

| Family                                                                                                                    | ภาพ/จังหวะที่ต้องส่ง                                                                            | Reject                                                                     |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Melee/cone/line (Cleave, Impale, Venom Spray, Shield Bash, Ground Slam, Whirlwind, Piercing Shot)                         | weapon sweep/thrust ที่ bake มากับ body ตาม committed sector/line; contact ต่อ actual recipient | วงเต็ม, ทิศตาม target หลัง lock, contact ด้านหลัง, weapon ลอยหมุนแยกชั้น   |
| Burst/projectile (Water Ball, Double Strike, Split Shot, Ice Lance, Arrow Shower, Chain Lightning, Overload)              | จำนวนลูก/จังหวะตาม canonical row; one aim/one cast; contact แยกตาม receipt                      | one projectile + fake flashes, clone slash พร้อมกัน, ลูกศรตั้งแต่ release  |
| Fields/nova/status/aura (Storm Field, Poison Cloud, Blizzard, Sand Storm, Firestorm, Meteor, novae, buff/curse/heal/aura) | bed/field ตาม footprint และ duration จริง; pulse/aura loop; status accent ตาม first-success     | field ที่ดู damage ตลอด, cloud ตาม target, aura ring กลายเป็น enemy radius |
| Basic/mob paths                                                                                                           | ใช้ contract เดียวกัน; mob skill ต้องอ่านทิศ/พื้นที่จริง                                        | coverage จาก manifest entry โดยไม่มี runtime หลักฐาน                       |

- Burst budget ใช้ count × authored share จริง; cosmetic fragments ไม่เพิ่ม hit
- Field: 1 active instance ต่อ caster+skill+arena; pulse ตาม absolute schedule; recast replace future work โดยไม่ refund
- Contact/impact/status อ่าน receipt จริง; visual cue ไม่สร้าง gameplay

## 6. Density และ timing

### 6.1 Visual timing envelope

| Family                  | Primary cue                         | Tail/ambient                      |
| ----------------------- | ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------- |
| Single melee cut/thrust | 100–160 ms active, contact 60–90 ms | trail dissolve 80–140 ms          |
| Shield/blunt            | contact 60–100 ms                   | recoil/particles 120–180 ms       |
| Venom Spray             | fan burst 160–240 ms                | droplets 120–180 ms               |
| Ground burst/nova/slam  | footprint peak 180–260 ms           | dust/cracks 250–450 ms            |
| Single projectile       | release 30–50 ms                    | impact 60–100 ms, exit 100–160 ms |
| Chain                   | one link ต่อ hop                    | decay 60–100 ms                   |
| Persistent field        | activation 180–250 ms               | bed/wind loop 0.8–1.6 s           |
| Mobile channel          | rotation ตลอด channel               | finish 120–180 ms                 |
| Buff/curse              | activation 180–250 ms               | exit 120–180 ms                   |
| Aura                    | enable cue                          | orbit 1.8 s, breathing 2.4 s      |

ค่าเหล่านี้เป็น presentation tuning ไม่ใช่ gameplay timing; runtime อ่าน resolved timestamps จริง

### 6.2 Density

```text
referenceArea = PI * 3m * 3m
densityScale = min(actualWorldArea / referenceArea, 2)
ambientBirthRate = familyBaseRate * densityScale * qualityMultiplier
activeCosmeticCap = ceil(familyBaseCap * densityScale * qualityMultiplier)
```

- `actualWorldArea`: circle πR², cone αR²/2 (radians), line L×W
- Quality: standard 1 / low 0.5; ลดเฉพาะ decoration ไม่ลด field bed/real pulse cue
- Cap เฉพาะ weather/decorative particles ไม่ใช่ hit recipients
- Budget รวมทั้ง arena: active cosmetic particles ≤ 2,000 และ effect instances ≤ 120 ที่ standard; stress scene = mob cap + 3 field + weather 1 ระบบ
- Birth schedule จาก absolute sim time + index + stable cosmetic seed; seek/resume ไม่ปล่อย backlog

## 7. QA และ acceptance

- ตรวจ source/atlas: alpha, cell grid, anchors, sockets, animation frames, metadata และ provenance; `python tools/check-authored-vfx.py --selected` สำหรับ selected VFX
- ตรวจใน arena/browser จริงที่ 1920 × 1080 ด้วย arena matrix: actor-to-area ratio, 8 world directions + mid-angle, motion/weapon alignment, center-to-edge coverage, empty ground, contact timing เทียบ receipt, overlap/occlusion, readability, interruption และ reduced motion
- ตรวจ pixel art ที่ native res และเทียบ reference; ภาพนิ่ง/lab preview เพียงอย่างเดียวไม่ผ่าน
- Performance: production live p50/p95, heap, device/browser; gate 60 Hz floor (p95 ≤16.8 ms, owner-accepted); dev showcase debug ไม่ใช่หลักฐาน
- Automated capture: screenshot ต่อ skill × 8 direction + mid-angle ที่ seed/เวลาเดิม เก็บ artifact คู่ version
- Mixed 2.5D slices ต้องผ่าน visual coherence check; rollback version ก่อนได้ทันที

## 8. Definition of done

- Proof มี character/mob/terrain slice, skill set, runtime integration และ provenance ที่ทำซ้ำได้ พร้อม browser evidence
- Pixel appearance และ chibi detail สอดคล้อง reference; camera และ 8 ทิศ + มุมกลางอ่าน action ได้; ทุก character ใช้ pose matrix เดียวกัน
- Baked single-sprite anchor/depth/full area/timing/contact/cancellation/reduced motion ผ่าน; ไม่มี separate weapon layer; ไม่เพิ่ม gameplay effects
- Performance และ selected versions/paths/checks/limits ถูกบันทึก; 2.5D ที่ยัง pending แยกจากของเดิมชัดเจน
- ลำดับ Character → Mob → Skill VFX → Map ครบ; ไม่มี geometry/runtime renderer ใน pipeline

# ModWorld — agent working agreement

Single-player, browser-only idle RPG; no server. This is the shared entry point for every coding agent.

| `art-reference/`                                                | Portable map art reference kit, generated-image holding area awaiting approval, concept images and map calibration snapshots; never imported by game runtime (dev review + tests only) | Generating, measuring or QC-ing map art; generated files are not game-ready until approved and copied into game assets; refresh with `art-reference/map/refresh.ps1` |
| `art/`                                                          | Generated gallery output (`gallery.html`, `favs.json` queue); never hand-edited, rebuilt by `tools/gallery.ts`                                                                         | Reviewing shelf sheets in a browser                                                                                                                                  |
