| `game/src/wiki/pages.ts`                                        | Player-facing wiki source                                                                                                                                                              | Changing what the wiki explains                                                                                                                                      |

Each fact has one owner. Link to it rather than copying it. Provider entry files import or point here; they carry no separate project rules.

## Default working skill

For repository implementation, fixes, reviews and investigation, apply [lean-agent](.agents/skills/lean-agent/SKILL.md) by default. Read it once when needed; reuse it if already loaded. No manual invocation is required. Explicit user requests for another approach or more detail take precedence. Tool policy stays here; the skill owns implementation and communication habits.

## Scope and documentation

- The current user request can change earlier design choices. Documents describe the current design, not permanent restrictions. Do not ask again solely because a requested change differs from an old design.
- UI-only work starts from components/styles and does not require formula or game-rule documents.
- Keep UI appearance and placement in code. Do not document button positions, colours, spacing, control inventories or other changing visual details.
- Edit docs only when requested, or when this task changes a documented formula, term, behavior contract or integration point that future work relies on. Patch that section only; no incidental reorganization, changelogs or unrelated rewrites.
- Skills and audit prompts follow this scope; they create no extra approval steps, documentation work or redesigns outside the task.
- Production art and art generation are first-party. Do not add third-party asset packs or external generation services (for example PixelLab). Existing imported reference packs stay as reference/placeholder only unless the user asks to remove them.
- Active-skill VFX follows [the authored VFX production queue](game/public/fx/skill-pool/vfx-production.md). The user requested the listed 23 attack skills completed and integrated together, without per-skill approval; skills outside that batch retain their existing effects.
- Work only in the active workspace/sandbox and on files supplied for the task. The current local files are the source of truth. Do not inspect Git state, history, branches, remotes or other worktrees; do not compare the workspace with committed content.
- Preserve in-flight changes. Plan briefly for risky/cross-layer work; implement straightforward changes directly. Delegate only independent work with nonoverlapping ownership when delegation is authorized.
- Ask about unclear scope, new dependencies, destructive operations or unsafe/lossy compatibility changes. Routine choices and explicitly requested design changes need no extra approval.

## Tool calls

- Before calling, identify the missing fact or required action and how its result advances the task. Use existing evidence when sufficient; keep this reasoning internal.
- Start with the relevant path/symbol and a bounded output. Exclude dependencies, generated output and logs unless implicated. Read matching sections; expand only when evidence calls for it.
- Reuse verified reads and passing checks until affected inputs change or a concrete uncertainty remains. Do not poll unchanged state without a reason.
- Batch independent searches/reads in one call and inspect each result. Run dependent actions sequentially; do not create unnecessary parallel work.
- If output is truncated, narrow the query or select a useful slice. On failure, identify the cause before retrying; retry only with a changed approach or new evidence. Repeated failure without new evidence calls for reassessment or a blocker report.
- A failing check outside the changed surface, with no changed input that explains it, is baseline or in-flight work: report it and do not fix or rerun it repeatedly without new evidence or a user request. Preserve concurrent edits in shared files; if verification cannot be made repeatable, say so instead of treating the result as a regression.
- Follow the verification scope below. Stop when acceptance criteria and required checks are satisfied. Review an unexpectedly long tool sequence for avoidable work; a call count never justifies skipping essential verification.

## Temporary files and cleanup

- Prefer direct commands and in-memory processing. Create temporary files only when required by a tool or when they materially simplify the task.
- Put temporary files in one task-specific directory under the operating system's temporary directory, within permitted filesystem boundaries. If that location is unavailable, use one task-specific temporary directory inside the active workspace. Do not scatter scripts, screenshots, reports, logs or scratch files throughout the workspace.
- Keep requested deliverables in their intended project locations; do not treat them as temporary files.
- Track temporary files and background processes created during the task. Remove temporary files when no longer needed and before finishing; stop task-created helper processes when no longer needed. Keep services needed to use the requested result running and report them at handoff.
- Delete only files or directories created by the current task. Before recursive deletion, verify the resolved absolute target is inside the task's temporary directory. Never use broad cleanup patterns or delete pre-existing files as housekeeping.
- Do not create transcript files, duplicate source copies, backup files or permanent helper scripts unless the task requires them.
- Before finishing, review task-created artifacts and remove unused files. Report any temporary files or helper processes that could not be cleaned up, including their locations or identifiers and the reason.
- Efficiency and cleanup must not skip required verification or compromise existing work.

## Passive-tree node generation

Plan the route before adding the node. For every new or moved node, state its purpose — route, two-anchor loop, junction, or leaf — and the anchors it serves. A count ("15 per wing", "five per cluster") is an output of the design, never the reason to add a node.

- A live leaf must be a Notable or a Keystone. An ordinary node with one connection is filler; the build retires it and `TR17` fails the tree.
- Every live Normal must sit on a route between two anchors (Start, Notable, Keystone, Junction). A loop or run hanging off a single point with no anchor inside it is filler, even when every node has two connections.
- A Keystone is a leaf off exactly one Notable; it is never a through-route. A second Keystone may share that Notable's pocket, but never a route.
- Never add a node for the build to retire. The retired ids in `tools/data/tree-retired-baseline.json` are frozen save keys; a new retired id fails `TR18`.
- Run `node tools/tree.ts --checks` after the build; `TR17`–`TR19` are the purpose, retirement and keystone-leaf gates.

## UI integration

- Shared tokens: `game/src/styles/variables.css`; tag defaults: `base.css`; reusable appearance: `skins.css`; layout: component `<style>`. Read relevant tokens and the existing component. Keep static appearance in classes; inline bindings are for runtime values and HudLayout placement.
- UI icons use PNG shelf art drawn through `.icon-mask` so they keep `currentColor`; map glyphs use PNG shelf art inside the map SVG. Inline SVG remains for structural graphics (tree/map geometry, marker frames/leaders, charts, effects), not standalone UI icons.
- Map markers are a shelf PNG glyph in a circular medallion on a vertical leader from the hex centre; frame and leader use the hover-hex blue (`--es`). Never repaint terrain for marker work.
- Current shell: fixed 15 × 15 Hub Grid, shared `HudLayout` regions and one scroll owner per region. Added/moved regions update `HudRegionId`, `HUD_REGION_META`, `DEFAULT_HUD_LAYOUT` in `game/src/ui/hud/hud-layout.ts` and matching `App.svelte` wiring; backfill old saved layouts. Appearance inside regions follows the requested design.
- New panels connect through `PANELS`, `RAIL`, icon/label maps and keyboard actions in `App.svelte`. Reuse existing shared controls such as `CollapseToggle.svelte` where appropriate; choose Grid/Flex and composition for the task.
- Keep native semantics, labels, keyboard access and visible focus. Map arrows select adjacent Blocks; Enter walks or uses a known Waypoint, with selection announcements.
- Inspect actual components with HMR in the integrated browser at `http://localhost:5173/__showcase#showcase-field`, **1920 × 1080 only** unless another viewport is requested. ## Default working skill

For repository implementation, fixes, reviews and investigation, apply [lean-agent](.agents/skills/lean-agent/SKILL.md) by default. Read it once when needed; reuse it if already loaded. No manual invocation is required. Explicit user requests for another approach or more detail take precedence. Tool policy stays here; the skill owns implementation and communication habits.

## Scope and documentation

- The current user request can change earlier design choices. Documents describe the current design, not permanent restrictions. Do not ask again solely because a requested change differs from an old design.
- UI-only work starts from components/styles and does not require formula or game-rule documents.
- Keep UI appearance and placement in code. Do not document button positions, colours, spacing, control inventories or other changing visual details.
- Edit docs only when requested, or when this task changes a documented formula, term, behavior contract or integration point that future work relies on. Patch that section only; no incidental reorganization, changelogs or unrelated rewrites.
- Skills and audit prompts follow this scope; they create no extra approval steps, documentation work or redesigns outside the task.
- Production art and art generation are first-party. Do not add third-party asset packs or external generation services (for example PixelLab). Existing imported reference packs stay as reference/placeholder only unless the user asks to remove them.
- Active-skill VFX follows [the authored VFX production queue](game/public/fx/skill-pool/vfx-production.md). The user requested the listed 23 attack skills completed and integrated together, without per-skill approval; skills outside that batch retain their existing effects.
- Work only in the active workspace/sandbox and on files supplied for the task. The current local files are the source of truth. Do not inspect Git state, history, branches, remotes or other worktrees; do not compare the workspace with committed content.
- Preserve in-flight changes. Plan briefly for risky/cross-layer work; implement straightforward changes directly. Delegate only independent work with nonoverlapping ownership when delegation is authorized.
- Ask about unclear scope, new dependencies, destructive operations or unsafe/lossy compatibility changes. Routine choices and explicitly requested design changes need no extra approval.

## Tool calls

- Before calling, identify the missing fact or required action and how its result advances the task. Use existing evidence when sufficient; keep this reasoning internal.
- Start with the relevant path/symbol and a bounded output. Exclude dependencies, generated output and logs unless implicated. Read matching sections; expand only when evidence calls for it.
- Reuse verified reads and passing checks until affected inputs change or a concrete uncertainty remains. Do not poll unchanged state without a reason.
- Batch independent searches/reads in one call and inspect each result. Run dependent actions sequentially; do not create unnecessary parallel work.
- If output is truncated, narrow the query or select a useful slice. On failure, identify the cause before retrying; retry only with a changed approach or new evidence. Repeated failure without new evidence calls for reassessment or a blocker report.
- A failing check outside the changed surface, with no changed input that explains it, is baseline or in-flight work: report it and do not fix or rerun it repeatedly without new evidence or a user request. Preserve concurrent edits in shared files; if verification cannot be made repeatable, say so instead of treating the result as a regression.
- Follow the verification scope below. Stop when acceptance criteria and required checks are satisfied. Review an unexpectedly long tool sequence for avoidable work; a call count never justifies skipping essential verification.

## Temporary files and cleanup

- Prefer direct commands and in-memory processing. Create temporary files only when required by a tool or when they materially simplify the task.
- Put temporary files in one task-specific directory under the operating system's temporary directory, within permitted filesystem boundaries. If that location is unavailable, use one task-specific temporary directory inside the active workspace. Do not scatter scripts, screenshots, reports, logs or scratch files throughout the workspace.
- Keep requested deliverables in their intended project locations; do not treat them as temporary files.
- Track temporary files and background processes created during the task. Remove temporary files when no longer needed and before finishing; stop task-created helper processes when no longer needed. Keep services needed to use the requested result running and report them at handoff.
- Delete only files or directories created by the current task. Before recursive deletion, verify the resolved absolute target is inside the task's temporary directory. Never use broad cleanup patterns or delete pre-existing files as housekeeping.
- Do not create transcript files, duplicate source copies, backup files or permanent helper scripts unless the task requires them.
- Before finishing, review task-created artifacts and remove unused files. Report any temporary files or helper processes that could not be cleaned up, including their locations or identifiers and the reason.
- Efficiency and cleanup must not skip required verification or compromise existing work.

## Passive-tree node generation

Plan the route before adding the node. For every new or moved node, state its purpose — route, two-anchor loop, junction, or leaf — and the anchors it serves. A count ("15 per wing", "five per cluster") is an output of the design, never the reason to add a node.

- A live leaf must be a Notable or a Keystone. An ordinary node with one connection is filler; the build retires it and `TR17` fails the tree.
- Every live Normal must sit on a route between two anchors (Start, Notable, Keystone, Junction). A loop or run hanging off a single point with no anchor inside it is filler, even when every node has two connections.
- A Keystone is a leaf off exactly one Notable; it is never a through-route. A second Keystone may share that Notable's pocket, but never a route.
- Never add a node for the build to retire. The retired ids in `tools/data/tree-retired-baseline.json` are frozen save keys; a new retired id fails `TR18`.
- Run `node tools/tree.ts --checks` after the build; `TR17`–`TR19` are the purpose, retirement and keystone-leaf gates.

## UI integration

- Shared tokens: `game/src/styles/variables.css`; tag defaults: `base.css`; reusable appearance: `skins.css`; layout: component `<style>`. Read relevant tokens and the existing component. Keep static appearance in classes; inline bindings are for runtime values and HudLayout placement.
- UI icons use PNG shelf art drawn through `.icon-mask` so they keep `currentColor`; map glyphs use PNG shelf art inside the map SVG. Inline SVG remains for structural graphics (tree/map geometry, marker frames/leaders, charts, effects), not standalone UI icons.
- Map markers are a shelf PNG glyph in a circular medallion on a vertical leader from the hex centre; frame and leader use the hover-hex blue (`--es`). Never repaint terrain for marker work.
- Current shell: fixed 15 × 15 Hub Grid, shared `HudLayout` regions and one scroll owner per region. Added/moved regions update `HudRegionId`, `HUD_REGION_META`, `DEFAULT_HUD_LAYOUT` in `game/src/ui/hud/hud-layout.ts` and matching `App.svelte` wiring; backfill old saved layouts. Appearance inside regions follows the requested design.
- New panels connect through `PANELS`, `RAIL`, icon/label maps and keyboard actions in `App.svelte`. Reuse existing shared controls such as `CollapseToggle.svelte` where appropriate; choose Grid/Flex and composition for the task.
- Keep native semantics, labels, keyboard access and visible focus. Map arrows select adjacent Blocks; Enter walks or uses a known Waypoint, with selection announcements.
- Inspect actual components with HMR in the integrated browser at `http://localhost:5173/__showcase#showcase-field`, **1920 × 1080 only** unless another viewport is requested. Use one visible tab; close it after verification. Playwright is not installed in this repository — never launch a standalone/headless browser or build a mirror; verify UI with the dev server, focused tests and `npm --prefix game run check`, using whichever browser the session already provides, and report the failure if none is available.
- For HUD placement also use `#panel-hud-layout-studio`: **Studio Apply** previews; **game Apply** saves. Verify the live region moves. Change shared layout machinery when the task calls for it, preserving working interactions and saved-layout compatibility.

| `engine/`, `game/src/`                                          | Implementation, interfaces and UI appearance                                                                                                                                           | Working on the affected code                                                                                                                                         |
| `game/src/icon/`                                                | Art shelf for item, skill, mob, UI and map-glyph images; folders group by subject and resolvers key on the file name                                                                   | Adding or sorting artwork                                                                                                                                            |
| `game/src/ui/combat/arena/`, `game/src/ui/combat/fx-manifests/` | Runtime animation + VFX manifests embedded by import; data, not shelf art                                                                                                              | Changing arena animation or authored VFX                                                                                                                             |
| `game/src/wiki/pages.ts`                                        | Player-facing wiki source                                                                                                                                                              | Changing what the wiki explains                                                                                                                                      |

Each fact has one owner. Link to it rather than copying it. Provider entry files import or point here; they carry no separate project rules.

## Code and data ownership

| Location                                | Responsibility                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `engine/`                               | Shared formulas and data-driven mechanics                                                                                                                                                |
| `tools/data/engine.json`                | Stats, combat, loot, craft, mobs/zones, inventory, fieldwork and dungeon configuration                                                                                                   |
| `tools/data/spawns.json`                | Field spawn layout, population cap, per-slot respawn, aggro/assist/leash ranges and offline engagement share                                                                             |
| `tools/data/mods.json`                  | Mod ranges, quality bands and drop weights                                                                                                                                               |
| `tools/data/town.json`                  | Town stock/prices, Standing, Collector, tasks, trade, Haggling, Delivery and Black Market                                                                                                |
| `tools/data/skills.json`                | Skill roster, reserve tiers and skill configuration                                                                                                                                      |
| `tools/data/mob-skills.json`            | Mob-only skill library and the Unique/Boss/Variant/Species override kits                                                                                                                 |
| `tools/data/tree.json`                  | Passive-tree specification                                                                                                                                                               |
| `tools/data/tree-retired-baseline.json` | Frozen legacy retired node ids; update only for an intentional save migration                                                                                                            |
| `tools/data/bases.json`                 | Hand-maintained frames, slots and Mod pools; never generate by parsing docs                                                                                                              |
| `tools/data/map.json`                   | Presentation map layout, terrain and colours; never import in `engine/` or `game/src/`                                                                                                   |
| `tools/`                                | Cages, reports and shared readers; `tools/map.ts` generates the overlay                                                                                                                  |
| `art/`                                  | Generated gallery output (`gallery.html`, `favs.json` queue); never hand-edited, rebuilt by `tools/gallery.ts`                                                                           |
| `game/src/assets/`                      | Runtime non-shelf images (backgrounds, skins); not keyed by the icon resolver                                                                                                            |
| `game/src/engine/client.ts`             | Browser bridge to canonical JSON and shared engine factories                                                                                                                             |
| `game/src/sim/`                         | Runtime composition/state; `core/` sheet+loop, `combat/` fights+skills, `town/` markets+contracts, `gear/` loot+craft, `world/` map+field; `core/player.ts` composes the character sheet |
| `game/src/state/save.ts`                | Save loading, migration and persistence                                                                                                                                                  |
| `game/src/ui/`, `game/src/App.svelte`   | Components and application wiring                                                                                                                                                        |

Gameplay numbers live in data JSON, formulas in `engine/`; do not duplicate either in the client. New game-content filenames use lowercase hyphens. `skill.md`, `skills.md`, `SKILL.md` and `.opencode/skills/` are reserved for agent skills, not game content. Gate output is the run record; do not create transcript files.

## UI integration

- Shared tokens: `game/src/styles/variables.css`; tag defaults: `base.css`; reusable appearance: `skins.css`; layout: component `<style>`. Read relevant tokens and the existing component. Keep static appearance in classes; inline bindings are for runtime values and HudLayout placement.
- UI icons use PNG shelf art drawn through `.icon-mask` so they keep `currentColor`; map glyphs use PNG shelf art inside the map SVG. Inline SVG remains for structural graphics (tree/map geometry, marker frames/leaders, charts, effects), not standalone UI icons.
- Map markers are a shelf PNG glyph in a circular medallion on a vertical leader from the hex centre; frame and leader use the hover-hex blue (`--es`). Never repaint terrain for marker work.
- Current shell: fixed 15 × 15 Hub Grid, shared `HudLayout` regions and one scroll owner per region. Added/moved regions update `HudRegionId`, `HUD_REGION_META`, `DEFAULT_HUD_LAYOUT` in `game/src/ui/hud/hud-layout.ts` and matching `App.svelte` wiring; backfill old saved layouts. Appearance inside regions follows the requested design.
- New panels connect through `PANELS`, `RAIL`, icon/label maps and keyboard actions in `App.svelte`. Reuse existing shared controls such as `CollapseToggle.svelte` where appropriate; choose Grid/Flex and composition for the task.
- Keep native semantics, labels, keyboard access and visible focus. Map arrows select adjacent Blocks; Enter walks or uses a known Waypoint, with selection announcements.
- Inspect actual components with HMR in the integrated browser at `http://localhost:5173/__showcase#showcase-field`, **1920 × 1080 only** unless another viewport is requested. Use one visible tab; close it after verification. Playwright is not installed in this repository — never launch a standalone/headless browser or build a mirror; verify UI with the dev server, focused tests and `npm --prefix game run check`, using whichever browser the session already provides, and report the failure if none is available.
- For HUD placement also use `#panel-hud-layout-studio`: **Studio Apply** previews; **game Apply** saves. Verify the live region moves. Change shared layout machinery when the task calls for it, preserving working interactions and saved-layout compatibility.

## Commands and verification

Windows + PowerShell; forward slashes in code paths. Run commands from the applicable root or `game/` package.

- Development: `npm install`, `npm run dev`; **port 5173 only**. Check `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 5173` first. Reuse an existing server; never start a second or kill one to reclaim the port. `npm run lint` runs the conservative Biome baseline.
- Gameplay/data: relevant cages/tests and `npm run typecheck`; broaden checks when shared behavior changes. `npm run verify` runs all cages; `npm test` runs `game/tests/`.
- UI: typecheck, `npm --prefix game run check` (warnings fail), focused tests for changed behavior, `npm --prefix game run build` for the production bundle, and integrated-browser interaction/appearance checks for behavior/layout changes.
- Coverage (optional report): `npm --prefix game run test:coverage`; no threshold is enforced yet.
- Docs/comments only: inspect the edited files and local links; no gameplay suite or browser check.
- Wiki: `npm run wiki` when wiki source, displayed data/formulas or player-facing behavior changes. `docs/wiki/*.html` is generated; never hand-edit. UI-only changes do not trigger wiki rebuilds.
- Other generators: `npm run skills`, `npm run gallery`, or the relevant `tools/` entry point when its input changes.
- Verify correctness/compatibility, not prescribed balance or content counts. Do not gate pacing bands, prices, tuned windows, roster sizes or content quotas. Do not rerun passing checks without a relevant change or unresolved concern.

# Skill: polish-indent

# PolishIndent

Cut words, never character. Every line that goes must take away only repetition, not information or voice.

## Anchor first

Before editing, read one unedited sample of the same author or the same file's untouched half, and keep it open. Note what carries the identity:

- sentence length and rhythm — short declaratives, or long clauses with commas
- verb person and directness — "run this", "we decided", "you might try"
- punctuation habits — em dashes, no semicolons, no exclamation marks
- register — dry, blunt, playful, formal
- humour and deadpan asides
- the load-bearing vocabulary: a project's glossary terms are not synonyms

An edit that makes text _cleaner and blander_ failed, however short it got.

## The pass

1. Delete the scaffolding: the preamble, the restatement of the request, the recap of what was just said, "Note that", "It is important to", "In order to", "Basically", "Actually", hedges that carry no doubt.
2. One idea per sentence. A sentence doing two jobs becomes one, or two — whichever is shorter.
3. Prefer the specific over the general: name the file, the command, the metric, not "the relevant configuration".
4. Conditional over blanket. "Run the tests before shipping" becomes "Run the tests when the change touches `engine/`."
5. Cut a rule the model already follows. If removing it changes no behaviour, keep it removed.
6. Move, never paraphrase: numbers, tables, formulas, identifiers, file paths, commands, quotes, term names.
7. Keep one deliberate oddity per paragraph untouched. That is usually where the voice lives.

## Where the length is

For a skill description: shortest form that makes the trigger unambiguous — what it does, then when to reach for it. No summary of the method, no list of every sub-case.

For `AGENTS.md` and rules files: route by task type ("for X, read Y") instead of loading everything on every turn. Project facts, boundaries, and hard-won rules stay; vague guidance goes.

For task prompts: state the goal, the constraint, and the evidence that says it is finished. Do not narrate the steps the executor would choose anyway.

## Done when

- the text is measurably shorter and says everything the original said
- reading the polished text against the anchor, the voice is indistinguishable
- no line was cut that the author would notice missing
- every remaining line earns its place: it states a fact, a trigger, or a limit

## Never

- no register shift — blunt stays blunt, formal stays formal
- no adding emoji, exclamation marks, or connective filler to smooth a cut
- no replacing a project term with a plainer near-synonym
- no shortening that drops a number, a caveat, or a condition
- if the text is already tight, say so and change nothing

| Location                                | Responsibility                                                                                                                                                                           |
| --------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `engine/`                               | Shared formulas and data-driven mechanics                                                                                                                                                |
| `tools/data/engine.json`                | Stats, combat, loot, craft, mobs/zones, inventory, fieldwork and dungeon configuration                                                                                                   |
| `tools/data/spawns.json`                | Field spawn layout, population cap, per-slot respawn, aggro/assist/leash ranges and offline engagement share                                                                             |
| `tools/data/mods.json`                  | Mod ranges, quality bands and drop weights                                                                                                                                               |
| `tools/data/town.json`                  | Town stock/prices, Standing, Collector, tasks, trade, Haggling, Delivery and Black Market                                                                                                |
| `tools/data/skills.json`                | Skill roster, reserve tiers and skill configuration                                                                                                                                      |
| `tools/data/mob-skills.json`            | Mob-only skill library and the Unique/Boss/Variant/Species override kits                                                                                                                 |
| `tools/data/tree.json`                  | Passive-tree specification                                                                                                                                                               |
| `tools/data/tree-retired-baseline.json` | Frozen legacy retired node ids; update only for an intentional save migration                                                                                                            |
| `tools/data/bases.json`                 | Hand-maintained frames, slots and Mod pools; never generate by parsing docs                                                                                                              |
| `tools/data/map.json`                   | Presentation map layout, terrain and colours; never import in `engine/` or `game/src/`                                                                                                   |
| `tools/`                                | Cages, reports and shared readers; `tools/map.ts` generates the overlay                                                                                                                  |
| `game/src/assets/`                      | Runtime non-shelf images (backgrounds, skins); not keyed by the icon resolver                                                                                                            |
| `game/src/engine/client.ts`             | Browser bridge to canonical JSON and shared engine factories                                                                                                                             |
| `game/src/sim/`                         | Runtime composition/state; `core/` sheet+loop, `combat/` fights+skills, `town/` markets+contracts, `gear/` loot+craft, `world/` map+field; `core/player.ts` composes the character sheet |
| `game/src/state/save.ts`                | Save loading, migration and persistence                                                                                                                                                  |
| `game/src/ui/`, `game/src/App.svelte`   | Components and application wiring                                                                                                                                                        |

Gameplay numbers live in data JSON, formulas in `engine/`; do not duplicate either in the client. New game-content filenames use lowercase hyphens. `skill.md`, `skills.md`, `SKILL.md` and `.opencode/skills/` are reserved for agent skills, not game content. Gate output is the run record; do not create transcript files.

## UI integration

- Shared tokens: `game/src/styles/variables.css`; tag defaults: `base.css`; reusable appearance: `skins.css`; layout: component `<style>`. Read relevant tokens and the existing component. Keep static appearance in classes; inline bindings are for runtime values and HudLayout placement.
- UI icons use PNG shelf art drawn through `.icon-mask` so they keep `currentColor`; map glyphs use PNG shelf art inside the map SVG. Inline SVG remains for structural graphics (tree/map geometry, marker frames/leaders, charts, effects), not standalone UI icons.
- Map markers are a shelf PNG glyph in a circular medallion on a vertical leader from the hex centre; frame and leader use the hover-hex blue (`--es`). Never repaint terrain for marker work.
- Current shell: fixed 15 × 15 Hub Grid, shared `HudLayout` regions and one scroll owner per region. Added/moved regions update `HudRegionId`, `HUD_REGION_META`, `DEFAULT_HUD_LAYOUT` in `game/src/ui/hud/hud-layout.ts` and matching `App.svelte` wiring; backfill old saved layouts. Appearance inside regions follows the requested design.
- New panels connect through `PANELS`, `RAIL`, icon/label maps and keyboard actions in `App.svelte`. Reuse existing shared controls such as `CollapseToggle.svelte` where appropriate; choose Grid/Flex and composition for the task.
- Keep native semantics, labels, keyboard access and visible focus. Map arrows select adjacent Blocks; Enter walks or uses a known Waypoint, with selection announcements.
- Inspect actual components with HMR in the integrated browser at `http://localhost:5173/__showcase#showcase-field`, **1920 × 1080 only** unless another viewport is requested. Use one visible tab; close it after verification. Playwright is not installed in this repository — never launch a standalone/headless browser or build a mirror; verify UI with the dev server, focused tests and `npm --prefix game run check`, using whichever browser the session already provides, and report the failure if none is available.
- For HUD placement also use `#panel-hud-layout-studio`: **Studio Apply** previews; **game Apply** saves. Verify the live region moves. Change shared layout machinery when the task calls for it, preserving working interactions and saved-layout compatibility.

## Commands and verification

Windows + PowerShell; forward slashes in code paths. Run commands from the applicable root or `game/` package.

- Development: `npm install`, `npm run dev`; **port 5173 only**. Check `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 5173` first. Reuse an existing server; never start a second or kill one to reclaim the port. `npm run lint` runs the conservative Biome baseline.
- Gameplay/data: relevant cages/tests and `npm run typecheck`; broaden checks when shared behavior changes. `npm run verify` runs all cages; `npm test` runs `game/tests/`.
- UI: typecheck, `npm --prefix game run check` (warnings fail), focused tests for changed behavior, `npm --prefix game run build` for the production bundle, and integrated-browser interaction/appearance checks for behavior/layout changes.
- Coverage (optional report): `npm --prefix game run test:coverage`; no threshold is enforced yet.
- Docs/comments only: inspect the edited files and local links; no gameplay suite or browser check.
- Wiki: `npm run wiki` when wiki source, displayed data/formulas or player-facing behavior changes. `docs/wiki/*.html` is generated; never hand-edit. UI-only changes do not trigger wiki rebuilds.
- Other generators: `npm run skills` or the relevant `tools/` entry point when its input changes.
- Verify correctness/compatibility, not prescribed balance or content counts. Do not gate pacing bands, prices, tuned windows, roster sizes or content quotas. Do not rerun passing checks without a relevant change or unresolved concern.

## UI integration

- Shared tokens: `game/src/styles/variables.css`; tag defaults: `base.css`; reusable appearance: `skins.css`; layout: component `<style>`. Read the tokens and the component. Keep static appearance in classes; inline bindings are for runtime values and HudLayout placement.
- UI icons: PNG shelf art through `.icon-mask` (`currentColor`); map glyphs: PNG shelf art in the map SVG. Inline SVG is structural graphics only (tree/map geometry, marker frames/leaders, charts, effects), not standalone UI icons.
- Map markers: shelf PNG glyph in a circular medallion on a vertical leader from the hex centre; frame/leader use hover-hex blue (`--es`). Never repaint terrain for markers.
- Current shell: fixed 15 × 15 Hub Grid, shared `HudLayout` regions, one scroll owner per region. Added/moved regions update `HudRegionId`, `HUD_REGION_META`, `DEFAULT_HUD_LAYOUT` in `game/src/ui/hud/hud-layout.ts` plus `App.svelte` wiring; backfill old layouts.
- New panels wire through `PANELS`, `RAIL`, icon/label maps, keyboard actions in `App.svelte`. Reuse shared controls like `CollapseToggle.svelte`.
- Keep native semantics, labels, keyboard access, visible focus. Map arrows select adjacent Blocks; Enter walks or uses a known Waypoint, with selection announcements.
- Inspect components with HMR at `http://localhost:5173/__showcase#showcase-field`, **1920 × 1080 only** unless requested. One visible tab; close it after verification. Playwright is not installed — never launch a standalone/headless browser or mirror; verify with the dev server, focused tests, `npm --prefix game run check`, or report no browser available.
- For HUD placement use `#panel-hud-layout-studio`: **Studio Apply** previews, **game Apply** saves. Verify the live region moves; preserve interactions and saved-layout compatibility.

/* icon-label: the small token-sized icon beside a label or table cell. */
.icon-label {
width: var(--icon-label);
height: var(--icon-label);
object-fit: contain;
flex: none;
}

/* glyph: a PNG UI symbol drawn in the current ink. Icons and symbols are images; inline SVG is

- reserved for structural graphics (tree/map geometry, charts, effects), never a standalone glyph. */
  .icon-mask {
  display: inline-block;
  width: var(--icon-label);
  height: var(--icon-label);
  flex: none;
  background: currentColor;
  -webkit-mask: var(--glyph) center / contain no-repeat;
  mask: var(--glyph) center / contain no-repeat;
  }

# Monster art references

This folder stores reference and candidate art. It is not the game asset shelf; approved animation atlases are copied to `game/public/combat/arpg/`.

## Layout

```text
art-reference/monsters/
  production-roster.json
  README.md
  animation-prompt-template.md
  <species>/
    animation/
    <style-variant>/
  _shared/collection/reference.png
```

- `<species>` is the canonical species id.
- `animation/` is a first-party animation set.
- `<style-variant>/` is a third-party reference pack, named in full (`spear-goblin`, `stone-golem`, `shadow-wolf`, `sword-shield`), never a bare suffix such as `spear` or `stone`.
- `_shared/collection/reference.png` is the one shared style reference.
- `animation-prompt-template.md` is the copy-ready generation and revision
  workflow. New animation must use its single-frame intake (Step 2b) with
  `tools/monster-animation-compose.py`; grid atlases are accepted only for
  drafts already under review.
- `production-roster.json` is the index of species status and animation paths.

## Required variant layout

Every variant must contain `meta.json`.

A first-party animation variant must contain:

```text
<species>/animation/
  meta.json
  atlas/animation.png
  source/            optional: concept or source image
  clips/             optional: per-action strips
```

Keep generated atlases under review as `atlas/animation-draft.png` and set `meta.json` status to `draft-review`. Promote a draft to `atlas/animation.png` only after its base and atlas are approved and its frame bounds are recorded.

Named gameplay variants from `tools/data/engine.json` (`mob.variants`) keep their own first-party set under:

```text
<species>/variants/<variant-id>/
  meta.json
  atlas/animation-draft.png
```

Use a lowercase-hyphen slug of the canonical variant name for `<variant-id>`. A named variant folder is not a version folder; keep one current set per named variant.

A third-party reference variant must contain:

```text
<species>/<style-variant>/
  meta.json
  source/reference.png
  clips/idle.png
  clips/walk.png
  clips/attack.png
  clips/hit.png      optional: only when the pack ships a recoil clip
  clips/death.png
  atlas/             optional: full sheet if the pack provides one
```

`frames/<clip>/000.png` is optional and only used when raw frames exist. Clip names are always `idle`, `walk`, `attack`, `hit`, `death`. Keep one current set per variant; do not add version folders.

# Monster animation prompt template

Use the species block and approved references for every run. The roster below is for species-level baseline atlases. For named gameplay variants, use each row in `tools/data/engine.json` at `mob.variants` and generate one image per named variant. Do not combine two species or two variants in one image.

## Target roster

Create one atlas for each of these 20 canonical species, in this order. The identifier is the canonical species id from `production-roster.json`:

1. `goblin` — Goblin
2. `orc` — Orc
3. `kobold` — Kobold
4. `ogre` — Ogre
5. `troll` — Troll
6. `minotaur` — Minotaur
7. `skeleton` — Skeleton
8. `mummy` — Mummy
9. `vampire` — Vampire
10. `demon` — Demon
11. `slime` — Slime
12. `golem` — Golem
13. `dragon` — Dragon
14. `treant` — Treant
15. `human` — Human
16. `lizardman` — Lizardman
17. `elf` — Elf
18. `giant` — Giant
19. `werewolf` — Werewolf
20. `dryad` — Dryad

Use the approved species design and references to fill the Species block for each run. Do not infer a complete design from the species name alone. If a species has no approved design block yet, define and review that block before generating its atlas.

## Named gameplay variants

For a variant batch, enumerate `tools/data/engine.json` at `mob.variants`. Generate one atlas per named variant, using the species id plus a lowercase-hyphen slug of the variant name as its folder key. Preserve the species anatomy and approved base design; use the variant name only for a restrained, readable palette or equipment cue. Keep every variant in a separate image and folder.

For named variant atlases, keep at least 24 transparent pixels between visible alpha and all four edges of every 256 × 256 runtime cell. Preserve complete poses inside that safe area; keep the feet on the existing ground anchor.

## Inputs

- **Image 1 — style and animation standard:** `game/public/combat/arpg/pixel-v2/player-animation-v2.png`; match its camera, sprite scale, atlas arrangement and frame canvas. Do not copy the Player's identity or equipment.
- **Body-angle reference:** the approved bases (`ogre/animation/source/base-v2.png`, `troll/animation/source/base-v3.png`) show the required whole-body rotation; match their torso/hip/leg orientation, not just the head.
- **Image 2 — approved base (optional):** `art-reference/monsters/<species>/animation/source/base.png`; use only after the base is approved. Never use `game/src/icon/mob` painted icons.
- **Optional source:** `<path to an approved concept or previous variant>`
- **First pass:** when no approved base exists, generate from the written species block only; do not attach the mob icon shelf.

## Species block

```text
Species id: <species>
Species name: <name>
Silhouette: <body plan, limb count, tail/wings/horns, posture>
Head ratio: <head height as a fraction of visible body height>
Face: <species-specific deviations from the shared Face language below — ear shape, snout/beak, mouth/tusks; keep the glowing eyes, low detail and upper-left lighting. Tusks are optional per species>
Equipment: <weapon, shield, armour, clothing; write "none" if none>
Locomotion: <walk gait for a four-legged / biped / hover body>
Attack: <one readable attack; state windup and contact>
Hit reaction: <how the body recoils without moving its feet>
Death: <how the body falls and settles>
Forbidden extras: <anything this species must never carry>
```

## Face language (shared)

Every species uses the same chibi goblin face language, adapted to its anatomy:

- **Structure:** oversized chibi head; large pointed ears where the species has ears; short broad nose; wide mouth. Add two small sharp tusks only where the species has them. Adapt the ears, nose and mouth to the species (beak, snout, mandibles) but keep the same simple readable face.
- **Eyes:** bright glowing eyes with a crisp inner highlight; pick a species-appropriate glow colour (ember orange, toxic green, cold blue, violet, etc. — not always yellow) with no outer glow halo, aura or lens flare. This is a mandatory checkpoint for every non-Slime species; verify the glow at the final 56–64 px size.
- **Detail:** low. Large flat colour areas; no warts, wrinkles, pores, scars, extra facial lines or busy texture.
- **Lighting:** fixed upper-left light. Flat highlight plane on the forehead, left cheekbone, nose bridge and chin; shadow under the brow, beside the nose, under the lower lip and along the jaw. Two to three shades per material, chunky pixel clusters.
- **Expression:** fierce and ugly, never cute or soft.
- **Species exception — Slime:** use a round, friendly blue slime face with large dark eyes and a small mouth (Rimuru-inspired), not the fierce goblin face. Keep every other shared face rule.

The approved reference is `art-reference/monsters/ogre/animation/source/base-v2.png`.

## Step 1 — static base pose (generate first)

Generate one neutral base pose and wait for approval before any animation. This is the identity reference for every later frame.

- Output a single 1024 × 1024 PNG.
- Treat the canvas as one 128 × 128 logical cell upscaled 8× with crisp 8 × 8 pixel blocks.
- Character 56–64 logical pixels tall, feet at logical y=108, whole body in a three-quarter view facing down-right (south-east/east): near shoulder and hip forward, far side receding, chest foreshortened, feet staggered. Not a front-facing torso with only the head turned; centred.
- Hard alpha only; transparent outside the silhouette.
- Save the approved image as `source/base.png` (normalized 128 × 128) and keep raw generations as `source/base-v*.png`.

```text
Create ONE static neutral base-pose sprite for a dark-fantasy MMORPG monster, to be animated later. Image 1 is the visual-style reference only: match its compact chibi silhouette, low visual density, flat colour groups, sparse selective pixel outlines and small native pixel scale. Do not copy any creature, card, label or layout from it.

SPECIES
<Insert the completed Species block here, including Face.>

OUTPUT CONTRACT
- One transparent RGBA PNG, 1024 × 1024.
- One 128 × 128 logical sprite cell upscaled 8× with crisp 8 × 8 pixel blocks.
- Character 56–64 logical pixels tall, feet at logical y=108, centred horizontally.
- Fixed mildly elevated three-quarter isometric camera, facing down-right (south-east/east), upper-left light. Rotate the WHOLE body about 45° toward the viewer's right: near shoulder and hip forward, far side receding, chest foreshortened, feet staggered. Do not draw a front-facing torso with only the head turned.
- At most 12 opaque colours, about two flat shades per material; hard alpha only; no anti-aliasing, blur, gradients or dithering.
- No background, floor, shadow, scenery, effects, text, watermark, border or checkerboard.
- Exactly one sprite; no extra poses, weapons or accessories.

Return only the transparent base-pose PNG.
```

## Step 2 — animation atlas (after base approval)

````text
Create ONE production monster animation atlas for a dark-fantasy MMORPG. Image 1 is the approved Player animation atlas: match its view, scale, pixel-art rendering and 8×5 frame layout, but do not copy its identity or equipment. Image 2 is the approved static base pose for this species: preserve its identity, chibi proportions, face language, palette and camera. Do not use the painted mob icon shelf.

SPECIES
<Insert the completed Species block here.>

OUTPUT CONTRACT
- One transparent RGBA PNG.
- Match the Player atlas source canvas exactly: 1585 × 992 pixels, arranged as 8 columns × 5 rows. If the image generator returns a different size, record the actual dimensions in `meta.json` and keep the result in draft review; do not resize or promote it.
- The runtime frame canvas is 256 × 256 pixels with anchor (128,224), matching `player-animation-v2.json`. Record per-frame source bounds in `meta.json`; do not assume uniform 256-pixel source cells.
- All 40 cells occupied. No grid lines, labels or outer margins; keep at least 24 transparent pixels between each pose and every edge of its own cell, including below the feet.
- Draw at native pixel size with hard alpha edges: fully transparent or fully opaque pixels only. No anti-aliasing, soft alpha, blur, gradients, dithering or downsampling.
- At most 12 opaque colours total, with about two flat shades per material.
- Fixed mildly elevated three-quarter isometric camera and upper-left light for every frame. Keep the camera, projection and character scale fixed; change the facing by turning the whole body around its vertical axis. Torso, hips, limbs and feet must agree with the facing; a head-only turn is not a directional pose.
- Standing root anchor at local (128,224) in the 256 × 256 runtime frame. Keep the feet planted at that anchor in upright poses. The final death pose may lie low but must stay within its frame bounds.
- Match the Player atlas's visible sprite scale and keep the full silhouette inside its own cell, including weapons, tails, wings and ears. No pose may cross a cell edge, and the lowest foot pixel keeps clear space above the cell bottom so the feet are never cut by the frame crop.
- Preserve the same identity, scale, palette, equipment and camera in every frame.
- No shadows, floor, scenery, effects, trails, blood, text, watermark, borders, UI or checkerboard.

ROW ORDER
Row 0 — idle, eight distinct facings in this exact order: south (toward camera), south-east (toward camera-right), east (right-facing profile), north-east (away from camera-right), north (away from camera), north-west (away from camera-left), west (left-facing profile), south-west (toward camera-left). One neutral ready pose per facing. Match the Player's established game-direction convention. These are eight character facings under one fixed camera, not eight camera angles; diagonal views must be drawn as genuine whole-body diagonal facings, not rotated cardinal sprites.
Row 1 — one walk pose for each of the eight facings in the row order above. Use a species-appropriate gait and keep the root anchor stable.
Row 2 — one readable attack pose for each of the eight facings. Keep the weapon and equipment consistent with the facing.
Row 3 — one distinct hit-reaction pose for each of the eight facings. Feet stay planted in upright poses.
Row 4 — one defeated/death pose for each of the eight facings. Keep the body low and inside its cell.

This atlas contains 40 pose frames: 8 idle facings plus 32 action poses (walk, attack, hit and death in all eight facings). Each state has one pose per direction; do not add extra action frames.

## Step 2b — single-frame intake (required for all new animation)

Generate one pose per PNG and let `tools/monster-animation-compose.py` own the grid. A model that never draws a grid cannot bleed frames into each other; gutters then come from code, not from model obedience. Grid atlases (Step 2) remain valid only for in-flight drafts already under review.

Request 40 files named `000.png` … `039.png` in row-major order: idle, walk, attack, hit, death × south, south-east, east, north-east, north, north-west, west, south-west — or pass `--map` with an explicit index/action/direction list.

### Single-frame OUTPUT CONTRACT

- One transparent RGBA PNG per pose, exactly one connected opaque pose, hard alpha only (0 or 255, no semi-transparency), art clear of every source edge.
- Identical canvas size on all 40 frames; content boxes of upright poses share one ground line within tolerance (death poses are exempt).
- Content must fit the runtime cell minus the 24 px gutter on all sides (384 px cell → at most 336 × 336 above the ground anchor); the tool downscales by an integer factor with NEAREST only, never upscales, and rejects anything needing more than 4×.
- Feet planted at the declared anchor; do not resample, mirror or rearrange frames by hand — the tool places every content box bottom-centred on the anchor.

### Intake command

```powershell
python -B tools/monster-animation-compose.py --frames-dir <frames> --meta-base <base-meta.json> --out-dir art-reference/monsters/<species>/[<variant-id>/]
````

The tool fails closed (writes nothing) on any violation, writes `meta.json` + `atlas/animation-draft.png` as `draft-review`, then runs `monster-animation-qa.py` over the composed atlas. Promotion to `atlas/animation.png` and the game registry stays a human approval plus the existing runtime-repack path.

Every frame must be a real pose change, never a translated copy. Keep the weapon and equipment anatomically consistent. Return only the atlas PNG.

````

## Reject before saving

Reject the result and regenerate or revise if any of these fail:

- Canvas does not match the Player atlas's 1585 × 992 source canvas, or the 8 × 5 frame arrangement is unclear.
- The silhouette is not chibi (realistic proportions, small head, long limbs).
- The camera angle or projection changes between frames instead of keeping the fixed mildly elevated isometric view.
- An idle facing turns only the head, or a diagonal facing keeps the torso, hips, limbs or feet cardinal; the whole body must show the requested direction.
- The face is cute or loses the shared goblin-like facial language.
- The face is over-detailed (warts, wrinkles, pores, scars, extra lines) or the eyes do not read as glowing.
- The face lighting does not follow the upper-left highlight/shadow planes.
- The painted mob icon shelf or a third-party creature was used as identity.
- Any cell is empty, duplicated, or contains another pose fragment.
- A named variant has less than 24 transparent pixels between its visible alpha and any cell edge.
- A pose crosses into a neighboring frame or its source bounds cannot be recorded in `meta.json`.
- Any visible alpha is within 24 pixels of a cell edge, so the frame crop risks cutting the silhouette or pulling in a neighbour.
- Alpha has semi-transparent pixels.
- The root or ground line drifts between upright frames.
- Sprite scale differs materially from the Player atlas.
- Idle facings are not eight distinct directions.
- Any idle facing changes the camera angle instead of turning the character under the fixed camera.
- Diagonal idle facings are cardinal poses rotated or mirrored instead of distinct whole-body diagonal views.
- Any action row is missing one of the eight facings, duplicates another pose, or uses a mirrored cardinal pose as a diagonal.
- Colours exceed the palette budget or use gradients.
- Text, UI, shadows, scenery, grid lines, effects or extra equipment appear.

## Revision prompt

Use this only after the first atlas is otherwise correct:

```text
Edit Image 1. Preserve its exact canvas, all 40 frames, identity, scale, palette, camera, row order and transparent alpha. Change only <the single named defect>. Keep every other frame unchanged. The corrected frame must stay inside its own source bounds and keep the same logical frame canvas (256 × 256) and ground anchor (128,224). Preserve the idle/attack/hit/death pose contract. Do not add or remove frames, do not resample, and do not add text, effects, shadows or a background. Return only the corrected transparent atlas.
````

## Output placement

```text
art-reference/monsters/<species>/animation/
  source/base.png          approved static base (128×128, feet at y=108)
  source/base-v*.png       optional raw generations
  meta.json
  atlas/animation-draft.png generated atlas while it is under review
  atlas/animation.png      only after the base and atlas are approved
```

Set `meta.json` to the actual dimensions, frame size, anchor and status. Use `base-approved` until the atlas exists. Species-level baselines stay under `<species>/animation/`. Named gameplay variants use `<species>/variants/<variant-id>/meta.json` and `<species>/variants/<variant-id>/atlas/animation-draft.png`. Keep one current set per named variant; do not add version folders.

## Example species lines

These examples are starting points only. Fill a complete, species-specific block for every target in the roster before generating that species.

- **Spear Goblin:** “Compact upright goblin; head about one-third of visible height, pointed ears and short sturdy limbs. Hold one clear spear. Attack with a short forward thrust.”
- **Stone Golem:** “Broad stone torso and shoulders; head about one-fifth to one-quarter of visible height, set between the shoulders. Use a few large stone shapes. Attack with a heavy downward stone-fist slam.”
- **Skeleton with Sword & Shield:** “Thin skeleton; skull about one-quarter to one-third of visible height, with separated ribs and limbs. Keep one sword and one shield distinct. Attack with a short sword slash while the shield guards the body.”
- **Little Demon:** “Compact demon; head about one-third to two-fifths of visible height. Use small horns and wings to define its silhouette. Attack with a quick claw swipe.”

The ratios refer to visible character height, not the 128-pixel cell. Use the reference for visual language only; do not use the mob icon shelf as a character reference. Apply the shared Face language above; the approved Ogre base (`art-reference/monsters/ogre/animation/source/base-v2.png`) is the facial reference.

# Monster art references

This folder stores reference and candidate art. It is not the game asset shelf; approved animation atlases are copied to `game/public/combat/arpg/`.

## Layout

```text
art-reference/monsters/
  production-roster.json
  README.md
  animation-prompt-template.md
  <species>/
    animation/
    <style-variant>/
  _shared/collection/reference.png
```

- `<species>` is the canonical species id.
- `animation/` is a first-party animation set.
- `<style-variant>/` is a third-party reference pack, named in full (`spear-goblin`, `stone-golem`, `shadow-wolf`, `sword-shield`), never a bare suffix such as `spear` or `stone`.
- `_shared/collection/reference.png` is the one shared style reference.
- `animation-prompt-template.md` is the copy-ready generation and revision
  workflow. New animation must use its single-frame intake (Step 2b) with
  `tools/monster-animation-compose.py`; grid atlases are accepted only for
  drafts already under review.
- `production-roster.json` is the index of species status and animation paths.

## Required variant layout

Every variant must contain `meta.json`.
